<t3_code_instructions>
## T3 Code interaction mode: Default

Prefer making reasonable assumptions and carrying out the user's request. Ask a concise question only when a missing user decision would materially change the result. Treat this mode as active until T3 Code supplies a different interaction-mode instruction.

## T3 Code browser

When browser work was asked, `preview_*` is the browser you share with the user: `preview_status` first, then `preview_open` if no tab can be automated. Prefer snapshot locators over coordinates. Switch browsers only if the tools are absent or `preview_open` says unsupported, the user asks, or two preview calls fail on one step. Then quote the error and switch.

## T3 Code orchestration

Ordinary coding tasks need no T3 tools.

- Subagents: use your native tool when the child uses your provider, a model it offers and no settings beyond yours (Claude `Agent`, `run_in_background:false`; Codex `spawn_agent`, then wait). Use `delegate_task` for another provider's model, user-asked settings, a separate checkout (`isolation:"worktree"`), or `delegate_task` by name. A native type on another provider's model counts too. Background agent: `delegate_task`, never a background `Agent`. Workflow only when asked.
- Call `orchestrator_capabilities` once per thread, before the first `delegate_task`. Again only after an error or a user-named provider change. Settings go in `target.options`. Provider or model unavailable: say so. Never switch unasked or fall back to native tools, Workflow or CLIs. Never make a child's checkout in the shell or in `task`.
- Every new delegate review or re-check is a new `delegate_task` (brief, findings, objections), never a `t3_thread_send`. Fix small review findings yourself; start no delegate for them. When told to proceed without a delegate, or to run fewer, `task_cancel` the extras. Start no replacement.
- Follow a running delegate's `next`. Don't poll it (`task_status`, `sleep`, watchers, Monitor, ScheduleWakeup). Stop a delegate run you replace or no longer need with `task_cancel`, never `t3_thread_interrupt` on a `childThreadId`.
- As a subagent or child, do the work yourself. Start no subagents unless your task says to.

- `t3_thread_launch` and `create_threads` make new top-level threads, only when the user asks for a new thread. "Subagent", "delegate", and "parallel" never mean one. Worktree thread: set `workspaceStrategy`. Honor a requested base. Otherwise independent work uses the default branch as `remote/branch` with `startFromOrigin:true`; with no remote, use the local default. Required unpublished commits and dependent work use their local base. Shell worktrees don't bind it, and no checkout setup in its prompt. No `workspaceStrategy`: project root, not your worktree.
- Given a thread id, `t3_thread_read` it before you answer about it. Asked to settle a thread, this one too: `t3_thread_organize`.
- Another machine: `t3_environment_links` lists linked ones. Pass its `environmentId` and that machine's `threadId` to T3 tools.
- Unlinked ("delegate this to my vps"): `t3_environment_link` with a `hint` from the user's words, never a pairing code in chat. No link tools: say to enable Settings → Labs → Linked environments.
- In your reply, mention a thread by its `link`, verbatim, never a plain title or bare id.
- A login, token, PIN, pairing code or sudo password only the user can give: call `request_secret`, not a chat ask or a handoff. Not for access you have. Sudo: if `sudo -n <cmd>` needs a password, use `delivery: "file"` and run `sudo -S -p '' <cmd> < "$file"`; the password takes stdin, so give other input as a file argument. Asked only to schedule: `schedule_task` without running its prompt.
- T3 tools may load late. Try the name once before you call it absent.

### Visuals and preview

- Answer data with a trend or comparison with a chart and show any visual the user asks for here: pass an HTML file path or inline HTML to `html_preview`, then `html_render`. A screenshot on disk or a text description doesn't show it. Never start a server for it. Page tools write only on user request. Never use them to show results. Asked for an image to post, send or use elsewhere: a `.png` file and its path, never `html_render`.
- Never use `preview_*` unasked to verify or show your own edit. Use them when the current request asks for browser work, including recording edits, or names a page or tab. Don't repeat preview calls from an earlier turn. Public pages: web fetch or search unless browser work was asked; then preview tools only, no web fetch. Close a tab you opened before you reply, unless the user asked for it or uses it.

ACP fallback: if the T3 tools are absent and `T3_ACP_MCP_NODE` is present, call them through the terminal: `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$T3_ACP_MCP_NODE" ${T3_ACP_MCP_ENTRYPOINT:+"$T3_ACP_MCP_ENTRYPOINT"} acp-mcp-call orchestrator_capabilities '{}'` (`T3_ACP_MCP_ENTRYPOINT` is unset for a standalone executable). Delegate with `acp-mcp-call delegate_task '{"task":"...","target":{"providerInstanceId":"...","model":"..."},"mode":"async","clientRequestId":"..."}'`.
</t3_code_instructions>

<runtime_info>In case you're asked: you are running in T3 Code through the Grok harness, as grok-4.7. No need to mention this otherwise. You can embed images, video, and audio using Markdown image syntax with absolute file paths. Link every other file you cite or produce by its absolute path, as in [http.ts:42](/abs/path/http.ts:42), so the user can open it in T3 Code's files viewer.</runtime_info>

<pull_request_linking>
Link each PR you create, take over, or push to: link_pull_request, or link_pull_requests for several, full URL, every stack layer, as your next call. Host tools don't link for you. If linking fails, say so. Skip PRs you only read or review and PRs named only as background. Call watch_pull_request when asked to monitor or babysit, or when work you were asked to do, such as a merge, still waits on checks or reviews, even after an earlier unwatch. Finish any needed branch update and push first, then watch and end your turn. Otherwise act now or hand back. Delegated children never watch, even if the brief says babysit. After PR work, a child's last line is: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>. Links and watches persist across pushes. For PR waits, no sleep, loops, gh --watch, Monitor or ScheduleWakeup. Before handback, call unwatch_pull_request on any PR you watch.
</pull_request_linking>

1→# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --json number,title,body,labels,comments`.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
10→- **Make an issue a sub-issue of a parent**: `gh issue create --parent <parent> ...`, or `gh issue edit <parent> --add-sub-issue <child>` afterwards (`gh` 2.94+). Older `gh`: `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<parent>/sub_issues -F sub_issue_id=<child-db-id>` (database id, as in **Blocking** below). Without sub-issues, put `Part of #<parent>` at the top of the child body.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh issue create --blocked-by <n>,<n> ...` or `gh issue edit <child> --add-blocked-by <blocker>` (`gh` 2.94+). Older `gh`: `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Count open blockers**: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only; 0 means startable). `gh issue view <n> --json blockedBy` also lists closed blockers, so filter it: `--jq '[.blockedBy.nodes[] | select(.state == "OPEN")] | length'`.
- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: post the explanation with `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`, then `gh issue close <number>`. On an already-closed issue, `gh issue close --comment` drops the comment and still exits 0.

Infer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

File issues only into the user's own repo. Never file into `mattpocock/skills` (the repo these skills come from) unless the user owns it. In a fork, `gh` can default to the upstream parent, so before the first `gh issue create` of a session, check the target with `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner` and confirm it with the user if it is not their repo.
20→
## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number>`, then `gh pr view <number> --comments` (off a TTY, `--comments` prints only the comments, not the body), and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh api --paginate 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=open' --jq '.[] | select(.author_association | IN("OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR") | not) | {number, title, author: .user.login, author_association, labels: [.labels[].name]}'`.
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.
30→
GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Read it as in **Read an issue** above.
40→
## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (see **Make an issue a sub-issue of a parent**). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: see **Blocking** under Conventions.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (see **Count open blockers**, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.
50→- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

10→- **Make an issue a sub-issue of a parent**: `gh issue create --parent <parent> ...`, or `gh issue edit <parent> --add-sub-issue <child>` afterwards (`gh` 2.94+). Older `gh`: `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<parent>/sub_issues -F sub_issue_id=<child-db-id>` (database id, as in **Blocking** below). Without sub-issues, put `Part of #<parent>` at the top of the child body.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh issue create --blocked-by <n>,<n> ...` or `gh issue edit <child> --add-blocked-by <blocker>` (`gh` 2.94+). Older `gh`: `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Count open blockers**: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only; 0 means startable). `gh issue view <n> --json blockedBy` also lists closed blockers, so filter it: `--jq '[.blockedBy.nodes[] | select(.state == "OPEN")] | length'`.

- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: post the explanation with `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`, then `gh issue close <number>`. On an already-closed issue, `gh issue close --comment` drops the comment and still exits 0.

Infer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

File issues only into the user's own repo. Never file into `mattpocock/skills` (the repo these skills come from) unless the user owns it. In a fork, `gh` can default to the upstream parent, so before the first `gh issue create` of a session, check the target with `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner` and confirm it with the user if it is not their repo.
20→
## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number>`, then `gh pr view <number> --comments` (off a TTY, `--comments` prints only the comments, not the body), and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh api --paginate 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=open' --jq '.[] | select(.author_association | IN("OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR") | not) | {number, title, author: .user.login, author_association, labels: [.labels[].name]}'`.
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.
30→
GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Read it as in **Read an issue** above.
40→
## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (see **Make an issue a sub-issue of a parent**). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: see **Blocking** under Conventions.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (see **Count open blockers**, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.
50→- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

1→# SurveyBeat architecture

Workers, Durable Objects, D1, and Effect import rules.

## Data and workers

- System of record is one Durable Object per Organization.
- D1 holds only the global index and auth/email bookkeeping, never survey content.
- MainWorker serves the signed-in app and API.
10→- SubmissionWorker accepts answers with observability off.
- SiteWorker serves the static landing page.

## Domain and answer page

- Domain code is Effect 4.1.2 and must import from effect/Effect and effect/Schema, not the Effect 3 @effect/platform style.
- packages/domain depends only on effect.
- The answer page under apps/web/src/answer stays plain TypeScript and must not import React, Base UI, Foldkit, or the HTTP API client.

matches.content: - **Cloudflare's own processing.** The [privacy policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/) says that for End Users, Cloudflare "processes data on behalf of its Customers", including "IP addresses, traffic routing data". Personal data is stored "for a period of time that is consistent with the business purposes", with **no fixed number** for edge logs. Separately, "Network Data" is used to identify and block malicious activity. The often-quoted "25 hours" applies only to the 1.1.1.1 resolver, not to Workers or zones. The [GDPR FAQ](https://www.cloudflare.com/trust-hub/gdpr/) says log metadata contains limited personal data, "most often in the form of IP addresses".
- **Joining automatically by verified email domain (WorkOS JIT).** Deferred to Release 3 with SSO. Free-mail domains make it unreliable for small teams.

The Organization admin role (WorkOS's org-level `admin`) covers administration only: Teams, Leads, and People. Seeing a Team's Results, comments, or Actions requires a Membership in that Team, whatever the person's Organization role. Admins are often the people members worry about most. If the admin role could read every Team's Results, it would undercut "trust before features" and put leadership roll-ups (Release 3) in through a side door.

content.text:
This is a large orchestration task.

Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Gemini 4 Hydrogen will handle the work. Opus 5.5 will review. Nine GDPR issues are mapped out. These cover compliance readiness. They cover legal pages. They cover access and erasure rights. They cover offboarding and retention. They cover data minimization and audit logs.

Issue #313 covers the compliance documentation pack. Release 3 issues are research and grilling tasks rather than implementation. They include map work, Vercel and chat research, channel-agnostic delivery, question formats, MCP auth, and MCP tools. Issue #303 slices Release 3 into implementation issues after research and grilling are resolved and ADRs are merged.

Research and grilling tickets will close with ADRs and decisions. GDPR tickets will produce mergeable code PRs. The AGENTS.md workflow requires branching from origin/main, one PR per change, and squash-merging immediately after opening. Main branch requires check, privacy, e2e, and preview-privacy checks. This is massive work. The user explicitly wants Sonnet and Gemini as workers and Opus as reviewer via T3 delegate_task.

Isolation worktrees will prevent child delegate checkouts from conflicting. Running delegates will not be polled. Each review will spawn a new delegate_task. Small review findings will be fixed directly. The T3 orchestration path will be used instead of the native shipper. Parent issues need closer inspection to map dependencies and identify parallel implementation opportunities.

name: gdpr-data-handling
description: Implement GDPR-compliant data handling with consent management, data subject rights, and privacy by design. Use when building systems that process EU personal data, implementing privacy controls, or conducting GDPR compliance reviews.
---

# GDPR Data Handling

Practical implementation guide for GDPR-compliant data processing, consent management, and privacy controls.

10→## When to Use This Skill

- Building systems that process EU personal data
- Implementing consent management
- Handling data subject requests (DSRs)
- Conducting GDPR compliance reviews
- Designing privacy-first architectures
- Creating data processing agreements

## Core Concepts
20→
### 1. Personal Data Categories

| Category               | Examples                    | Protection Level   |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------ |
| **Basic**              | Name, email, phone          | Standard           |
| **Sensitive (Art. 9)** | Health, religion, ethnicity | Explicit consent   |
| **Criminal (Art. 10)** | Convictions, offenses       | Official authority |
| **Children's**         | Under 16 data               | Parental consent   |

30→### 2. Legal Bases for Processing

```
Article 6 - Lawful Bases:
├── Consent: Freely given, specific, informed
├── Contract: Necessary for contract performance
├── Legal Obligation: Required by law
├── Vital Interests: Protecting someone's life
├── Public Interest: Official functions
└── Legitimate Interest: Balanced against rights
40→```

### 3. Data Subject Rights

```
Right to Access (Art. 15)      ─┐
Right to Rectification (Art. 16) │
Right to Erasure (Art. 17)       │ Must respond
Right to Restrict (Art. 18)      │ within 1 month
Right to Portability (Art. 20)   │
50→Right to Object (Art. 21)       ─┘
```

## Detailed worked examples and patterns

Detailed sections (starting with `## Implementation Patterns`) live in `references/details.md`. Read that file when the navigation summary above is insufficient.

## Best Practices

### Do's
60→
- **Minimize data collection** - Only collect what's needed
- **Document everything** - Processing activities, legal bases
- **Encrypt PII** - At rest and in transit
- **Implement access controls** - Need-to-know basis
- **Regular audits** - Verify compliance continuously

### Don'ts

- **Don't pre-check consent boxes** - Must be opt-in
70→- **Don't bundle consent** - Separate purposes separately
- **Don't retain indefinitely** - Define and enforce retention
- **Don't ignore DSARs** - 30-day response required
- **Don't transfer without safeguards** - SCCs or adequacy decisions

180→- **MCP server.** A remote MCP server lets a lead use an AI assistant to ask about their teams' results and manage actions. It enforces the same permissions and privacy thresholds as the web app, because it calls the same domain services.
- **Webhooks.** Webhooks for "round results ready" and "action created or updated".

### 5.8 Product surfaces outside the app

- A marketing landing page, a pricing page that can be a placeholder, and legal pages for privacy, terms, and the data processing agreement. The old app had legal page stubs. The rebuild needs real text before any external customer uses it.
- Transactional emails for invitations, reminders, results-ready notices, and action updates. They must look good in the major email clients and in dark mode.

## 6. Platform and architecture

190→Everything runs on Cloudflare. No Next.js, no Vercel, and no separate cloud provider for compute or data. Sign-in runs on Better Auth inside the Main Worker, so the Slack and Microsoft Teams platforms are the only required external services.

### 6.1 Fixed technology choices

| Concern | Choice | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Infrastructure as code | alchemy.run | Every Cloudflare resource, binding, secret, and custom domain is declared in TypeScript with Alchemy. No dashboard changes. No Terraform. No hand-edited wrangler config. |
| Runtime | Cloudflare Workers | One Worker serves the API and the static web app (Workers static assets). Add more Workers only when a job needs a different runtime profile, such as a queue consumer. |
| Business logic | Effect | All domain logic, data access, and integrations are Effect programs. Errors, dependencies, retries, and timeouts are typed. Domain services are Effect services with layers that can be swapped in tests. |
| Schemas | Effect Schema | One schema definition per domain type is shared by the API, the client, the database layer, and the AI tool definitions. External data is parsed at the boundary, and internal code trusts the types. |
200→| HTTP API | Effect's platform HTTP API module | The API is declared once. The server implementation and a typed client for the web app both come from that declaration. |
| Web app | React single-page app built with Vite | Client-side routing with a typed router, such as TanStack Router. Answer pages and email landing pages must render fast without a heavy bundle. Split them into their own small entry point. |
| UI components | Base UI | Unstyled, accessible primitives. Build a small design system of your own on top (tokens, typography, and a dozen composed components). Tailwind CSS for styling is fine. Charts need an accessible library or hand-built SVG, and each chart needs a table view. |
| Authentication | Better Auth on D1, email codes | The Worker serves `/auth/*`: an email-code start and verify, a session cookie, and sign-out. The session is checked on every request against D1 and the Organization's Durable Object. ADR 0022 and ADR 0023. |
| Email | Cloudflare Email Service | Sends invitations, reminders, and notices. Inbound email routing is optional, for reply-to-answer later. If Cloudflare email sending cannot meet deliverability needs, decide on a fallback and record it. |
| AI | Cloudflare Workers AI, through AI Gateway | Comment redaction, theme grouping, discussion guides, and "ask your results". AI Gateway handles caching, rate limits, logging policy, and model swaps. Never send raw comments to a model that keeps them. |

### 6.2 Cloudflare building blocks and their jobs

The recommended layout follows. Departures are fine when they make the system simpler, but write down the reason.
210→
- **Durable Object per organization, with SQLite storage, as the system of record.** Each organization's people, teams, pulses, rounds, submissions, results, and actions live in that organization's own Durable Object. This gives hard tenant isolation, strongly consistent writes, and plain SQL for analytics within one organization. Survey data is small, so a single object's storage limit is far away. An organization with 5,000 people answering weekly for 5 years stays well under it. Check this number against current Cloudflare limits before you commit.
- **Durable Object per open round** (optional, decide during the build). It counts participation, rejects double submissions, and owns the round's state machine. If the organization object handles this load well, skip the extra object.
- **D1 for the global index.** This holds what must be looked up before you know the organization: auth user to Persons, invitation token to organization and round, Slack and Teams workspace to organization, and API keys. Keep it small. No survey content goes here.
- **Cloudflare Workflows for the round lifecycle.** Each round is a durable workflow. It waits until the open time, sends invitations in batches, waits, sends reminders, closes, computes results, and notifies. Workflows give retries and resumption after crashes, and each step must be idempotent.
- **Cron Triggers** run once an hour to create the next round for each active pulse. This job is idempotent. Running it twice creates no duplicate rounds.
- **Queues** buffer outbound messages (email, Slack, Teams) and inbound webhooks, with retries and a dead-letter queue.
- **R2** stores exports and generated PDFs, and backups of each organization's data on a schedule.
- **KV** holds rarely changing configuration and caches, if needed. Do not use it for sessions that must be revoked at once.
- **Workers Analytics Engine** stores product metrics (send counts, open rates, answer latency). It must never contain answers.
220→- **Turnstile** protects the public link answer page against bots.
- **Secrets Store, or Worker secrets managed through Alchemy**, holds the Slack and Teams credentials.

### 6.3 Code organization

- One repository and one package manager workspace. Suggested packages are the domain (pure Effect services and schemas, with no Cloudflare imports), the Cloudflare adapters (Durable Objects, D1, Queues, Workflows, and email, each implementing a domain interface), the API, the web app, the infrastructure definition, and the email templates.
- The domain package must run in plain Node tests without Cloudflare. Adapter packages are tested against local Cloudflare emulation (Miniflare, through Alchemy's dev mode or the Vitest integration for Workers).
- Organize modules by domain concept (rounds, privacy, results, actions), not by layer or execution step.

### 6.4 Environments and delivery
230→
- Alchemy stages give every pull request its own preview environment, with its own Workers, D1, and Durable Object namespaces. The preview is removed when the pull request closes.
- `staging` and `production` are Alchemy stages too. Production deploys from the main branch after CI passes.
- CI runs type checking, linting, unit tests, Worker integration tests, the privacy test suite, and an accessibility check on the answer page.
- Errors and traces go to Workers Logs and Workers Observability. Add Sentry only if Cloudflare's tooling is not enough, and then strip all answer content before sending.

## 7. Quality requirements

- **Privacy tests are release blockers.** The suite proves at least the following. An anonymous submission has no stored path back to a person. Every result view respects the minimum group size, including subtraction across groups. Logs from the submission path contain no identifiers. Exports and the MCP server obey the same rules.
- **Performance.** The answer page reaches first paint (the screen with the anonymity statement) in under 1 second and shows the first Question's text in under 1.3 seconds, measured as the 75th percentile on a mid-range phone. The text needs one round trip, because the Invitation token is only in the URL fragment (ADR 0005, ADR 0008). Answer submission completes in under 300 ms at the 95th percentile. The results page renders in under 1.5 seconds for a team with two years of weekly rounds.
240→- **Reliability.** No invitation is sent twice. No invitation is skipped silently. Failed sends show up in the lead's view with the reason.
- **Accessibility.** WCAG 2.2 AA on every page. The answer flow works with a screen reader and with a keyboard alone.
- **Testing approach.** Test behavior through the domain services and the API, not internal functions. Swap Effect layers for in-memory adapters in unit tests. Run a small set of end-to-end tests against a real preview stage, covering create pulse, receive invitation, answer from email, close round, see results, and create action.

## 8. Release plan

Each release is usable on its own. Ship a release to a real team (your own, first) before starting the next.

**Release 1. The core loop for one team.**
Sign-in with an email code, plus organization and team setup by hand. Pulses from templates, with rating, choice, and text questions. Weekly cadence with time zones. Email invitations with one-tap first answers, and reminders. Anonymous mode with the minimum group size. Round results with trends and sample sizes. Actions with owner and status, shown in the next invitation. The full privacy test suite. Preview environments per pull request.
250→
**Release 2. Insight.**
Comment redaction and themes. Discussion guide. Team health overview with action markers. Delayed sharing. The member's private history page. German translation, deferred: English only for now (ADR 0025).

**Release 3. Organizations.**
Enterprise SSO and Directory Sync. Nested teams and leadership roll-ups with subtraction-safe thresholds. Standard questions and cross-team comparison. Confidential mode. Audit log. Exports.

**Release 4. Where people already work.**
Slack app. Microsoft Teams app. Question rotation. Action follow-up questions.

260→**Release 5. Open up.**
Public API, webhooks, and the MCP server. "Ask your results". Issue tracker sync for actions.

## 9. Out of scope

- Individual performance reviews, 360 reviews, and anything that scores a single person. Those features change what members believe the tool is for, and they would erode trust in anonymous team health data.
- A general-purpose form builder. SurveyBeat asks short, recurring questions. Leads who need branching logic, file uploads, or 40-question forms should use a form tool.
- Industry benchmarks against other companies' data. Revisit this only when there is enough data and a legal basis to pool it.
- Native mobile apps. Email, chat, and a fast mobile web page cover the need.

270→## 10. Open questions for the product owner

These need a decision from the product owner. Each one has a default you can build against until someone answers.

1. Should members see raw comments, or only themes? Default is themes only, with the lead able to show raw comments if the minimum group size is met.
2. What is the default minimum group size? Default is 4, with 3 as the floor.
3. Is self-serve sign-up for small teams wanted, or is the product sold to organizations only? Default is self-serve, with an organization created at first sign-in.
4. Which AI models are acceptable for comment processing, given data residency? Default is Workers AI models only, through AI Gateway with logging of prompts turned off.
5. What is the target market's main chat tool, Slack or Microsoft Teams? This decides which one ships first in release 4. Default is Slack.
6. Is the "surveybeat.com" domain still owned and pointed at Cloudflare? The old Terraform config assumed so.

A discrepancy was found in SPEC.md §8.

Issue #295 re-sequences Release 3 ahead of enterprise Organizations. Issue #296 confirms this reordering. The merge goal includes nine GDPR implementation issues plus their parent tracking ticket.

The wayfinder grilling requires ADRs and SPEC updates before closing issues. GDPR work requires merged code PRs. The plan is to orchestrate in waves based on dependencies. Wave 1 will target unblocked work. GDPR code issues likely overlap and need file partitioning. Issue #305 on legal pages appears relatively independent.

Issue #313 is independent docs work. Issues #306 through #309 overlap on data subjects, deletion, and API changes. Issue #310 touches shared tables. Issue #311 is somewhat independent. Issue #312 spans new tables and call sites, so it overlaps everything. The GDPR wave needs a strategy to avoid merge conflicts.

The first wave will run in parallel worktrees. Issue #313 and #305 are the cleanest independent tasks. The grilling ticket #296 is the first gate. It updates SPEC §8. #297 and #301 are research tasks. They should not edit SPEC.md until decisions are made.

Wave 2 will run after #296 merges. It covers grilling issues #298 and #299. GDPR implementation can run in parallel with R3 research if files do not overlap. The GDPR stack will split by worker. Sonnet 5.5 will handle export, erasure, and offboarding as a tightly coupled PR stack. Gemini 4 Hydrogen will handle legal pages.

Issue #309 overlaps with erasure on the person model. The GDPR stack is now fully partitioned. Sonnet 5.5 will handle export, erasure, offboarding, and rectification as a sequential PR chain in one worktree. Gemini 4 Hydrogen will handle legal pages, retention jobs, token residency, audit log, and documentation.

Issue #312 overlaps with admin actions from #306 through #309, so it must merge after that stack. The audit log will be the final GDPR task. Issue #304 will close last once all child issues are done. Only two workers are available, so the entire backlog will be processed in waves without spawning extra models. The first wave of unblocked independent work will begin immediately.

The two workers will launch immediately on the highest-value unblocked slices. Sonnet 5.5 will handle the GDPR data-subject rights stack. Gemini 4 Hydrogen will handle the R3 research and grilling work that produces ADRs and documentation. The goal is to maximize parallel throughput while respecting file ownership boundaries.

The grilling and research tasks will be split into separate delegates. Each worker will own one issue at a time to keep reviews simple. Wave 1 is launching now with Sonnet 5.5 on #305 legal pages.

Four parallel worktree tasks are being launched now. Sonnet 5.5 will handle #305 legal pages and #297 research. Gemini 4 Hydrogen will handle #313 documentation. The overlap risk is managed by keeping each task in its own isolated worktree.

Issue #296 must merge first because it edits SPEC.md and gates the rest of Release 3. It will be assigned to one worker alongside research that does not touch the spec. The full issue bodies need to be fetched for accurate briefs. Existing ADR numbers must be checked to prevent collisions if workers create ADRs in parallel. The docs/adr directory will be read to verify numbering.

I will fetch the full bodies of the first-wave issues and review the acceptance criteria for the remaining GDPR tickets to finalize the dependency graph. I will check that main is green before launching any worktrees. I will use async delegate mode so I can sleep until the workers complete. I will only call ship-it or file-pr once a child branch is ready to merge.

Workers will implement and commit in isolated worktrees. They will not push or merge branches without explicit instruction. The shipper cannot see their commits unless they push. I will coordinate review with Opus 5.5 and then open the pull requests.

Workers will create branches from origin/main and implement issues fully. They will run tests, commit, and push to open pull requests against main. They must not merge. After Opus review, the orchestrator will merge. Workers will return the PR URL, a summary, and test results. They will follow the repository's AGENTS.md and gitbutler skill.

content.text:
## Goal

Bring SurveyBeat into full GDPR compliance before onboarding external EU Organizations, grounded in `SPEC.md` (§5.3, §5.6, §5.8), `GLOSSARY.md`, binding ADRs (`0001`–`0026`), and the `gdpr-data-handling` compliance checklist.

## What SurveyBeat already satisfies by design (Art. 25)

- **True anonymization of anonymous Submissions (Recital 26, ADR 0005):** `submission` and `answer` tables are `WITHOUT ROWID` with random 128-bit keys and store no Person, no Invitation, and no timestamp. `SubmissionWorker` keeps logs, traces, tail, and Logpush disabled (`preview-privacy` + canary sweep verify this).
- **Store-time Redaction (ADR 0009):** Organization roster names, emails, phone numbers, handles, and URLs are stripped before comments are stored; raw text is never persisted.
- **Minimum group size enforcement (ADR 0004):** Enforced per aggregate (default 4, floor 3) across every Result view, enforced by `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts` and `*.privacy.test.ts`.
- **EU zero-data-retention AI sub-processing (ADR 0015):** Opt-in per Organization (off by default), pinned to `google-vertex/europe` and `amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1` via OpenRouter with `zdr: true`, `allow_fallbacks: false`, `data_collection: "deny"`, receiving redacted comment text only.
- **Strictly necessary cookie only:** Only `__Host-surveybeat-session` (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/`). No third-party analytics, advertising, or tracking cookies exist on the app or landing page (`SiteWorker`).
- **Tenant & role isolation (ADR 0003, ADR 0006):** One Durable Object per Organization; Organization admins cannot read any Team's Results.

## Gaps to close

The sub-issues attached to this tracker cover the remaining legal, product, technical, and documentation requirements:

1. **Transparency & Legal Surfaces (Art. 12–14, Art. 28, SPEC §5.8, ADR 0015):** Public static Privacy Notice, Terms, DPA, and Sub-processor list on `SiteWorker`, plus updated in-app `/privacy` links.
2. **Right of Access & Portability (Art. 15, Art. 20, SPEC §5.3):** Self-service machine-readable JSON export of all personal data across D1 and Organization Durable Objects.
3. **Right to Erasure (Art. 17, SPEC §5.3):** True personal data deletion (scrubbing/removing PII across DO and D1 rather than soft-deleting via `removed_at`), while preserving non-personal anonymous Submissions and Results.
4. **Organization Offboarding (Art. 28(3)(g)):** Full tenant export and irreversible deletion of an Organization's Durable Object and all D1 index rows.
5. **Right to Rectification, Restriction & Objection (Art. 16, Art. 18, Art. 21):** Verified email updates, full Pulse invitation opt-out, and processing restriction flags.
6. **Storage Limitation & Automated Retention (Art. 5(1)(e), SPEC §5.3):** Configurable raw Answer/comment retention (default 24 months) and automated retention sweeps for `email_send`, `captured_email`, expired sessions/verifications, closed-Round invitations, and soft-removed People.
7. **Data Minimization & EU Data Residency Hardening (Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 25, Art. 44–49):** EU jurisdiction for D1 and Organization Durable Objects, removing Invitation tokens from `MainWorker` URL query strings (`/delivery`, `/unsubscribe`), and minimizing Better Auth session PII (`ipAddress`, `userAgent`) and unused plugin surfaces.
8. **Accountability & Audit Logging (Art. 5(2), Art. 7, Art. 32, SPEC §5.6):** Append-only privacy/admin audit log inside each Organization Durable Object (including AI opt-in & DPA acceptance provenance).
9. **Compliance Documentation Pack (Art. 30, Art. 33–35, Art. 28):** Checked-in RoPA, DPIA, 72-hour Breach Notification Runbook, Vendor DPA Register, and customer LIA template.

## Done when

Every sub-issue linked below is closed, all new endpoints are classified in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts`, and `pnpm test:privacy` proves that erasure, export, retention, and audit logging never weaken ADR 0004 or ADR 0005.
=====305=====
## Why

GDPR Articles 12–14 require clear, accessible, pre-collection transparency notices, and Article 28 requires a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and sub-processor disclosure for every customer Organization.

Today:
- `apps/web/src/site/render.ts` renders only `© 2026 SurveyBeat` in the landing page footer with no legal links.
- `SiteWorker` (`packages/cloudflare/src/SiteWorker.ts`) serves only `/` and `/app` — there are no public `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/dpa`, or `/subprocessors` pages.
- The in-app `/privacy` page (`apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts`) explains SurveyBeat's anonymity architecture, but omits legally required Art. 13/14 disclosures and the sub-processor list required by ADR 0015 (*"OpenRouter is a sub-processor (its DPA is part of its terms), and so are Google Cloud or AWS for the model call. Customer-facing privacy pages must name them."*).
- `SPEC.md` §5.8 states: *"legal pages for privacy, terms, and the data processing agreement. The old app had legal page stubs. The rebuild needs real text before any external customer uses it."*

## Scope

1. **Public static legal pages on `SiteWorker`** (prerendered into `apps/web/dist-site`, zero JS, strings in `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts` per `no-literal-ui-text`):
   - `/privacy` — Full GDPR Art. 13/14 Privacy Notice:
     - Controller/processor identity and privacy/DPO contact details.
     - Role distinction: customer Organization as controller and SurveyBeat as Art. 28 processor for Pulse/Team data; SurveyBeat as controller for sign-in, marketing site, and abuse prevention.
     - Every personal data category collected and its Art. 6 legal basis.
     - Plain statement that anonymous Submissions store no Person and no time (ADR 0005), are non-personal data under Recital 26, and therefore survive deletion (`SPEC.md` §5.3).
     - Retention periods for every category (raw Answers/comments default 24 months, aggregated Results, sessions, emails, 30-day point-in-time restore window per ADR 0005).
     - Cookie and browser storage disclosure: strictly necessary `__Host-surveybeat-session` cookie (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`), zero tracking/marketing cookies, and browser-local `localStorage` Edit key and kept answers (1-year TTL, clearable on `/history` per ADR 0017).
     - Data Subject Rights (Art. 15–22), how to exercise them (self-service + contact email, 30-day response deadline), and right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.
     - International data transfer mechanisms (SCCs / EU-US DPF) and EU-only ZDR AI routing (ADR 0015).
   - `/subprocessors` — Named sub-processor register with purpose, region, and DPA/transfer basis:
     - **Cloudflare, Inc.** (Workers, Durable Objects, D1, Queues, Email Sending).
     - **OpenRouter, Inc.** (AI routing when AI processing is turned on by an Organization admin; ZDR, zero prompt logging).
     - **Google Cloud (`google-vertex/europe`)** and **Amazon Web Services (`amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1`)** (EU-pinned inference endpoints for Comment themes and Discussion guides per ADR 0015).
   - `/terms` — Terms of Service.
   - `/dpa` — Standard Art. 28 Data Processing Agreement for customer Organizations (incorporating sub-processor authorization, TOMs, breach notification without undue delay, and return/deletion on termination).
2. **Link legal pages from every surface:**
   - Landing page footer (`apps/web/src/site/render.ts`).
   - App sign-in screen, authenticated shell footer/account menu, and in-app `/privacy` screen (`apps/web/src/app/App.ts`).
   - Answer page (`apps/web/src/answer/`) footer link within the ADR 0008 size budget (JS ≤ 10 KB gzip, HTML ≤ 8 KB, CSS ≤ 2 KB).
   - Transactional email footer (`packages/emails/src/Layout.tsx`).

## Done when

- `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/dpa`, and `/subprocessors` prerender cleanly into `apps/web/dist-site` and return 200 on `SiteWorker` with no JavaScript.
- Every ADR 0015 sub-processor and every GDPR Art. 13/14 disclosure item is present and accurate against the live codebase.
- Links exist on the landing page, dashboard app, answer page (passing `budget.test.ts` and Lighthouse gate), and email layout.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build` pass.

## Why

Beyond software controls, GDPR mandates written governance artifacts that supervisory authorities and enterprise EU customers request during vendor security/privacy reviews:
- **Records of Processing Activities (Art. 30)** — both as controller (auth/account/site) and processor (Art. 30(2) for customer Organizations).
- **Data Protection Impact Assessment (Art. 35)** — required when processing employee workplace feedback using automated/AI analysis (Comment themes & Discussion guides), given the power imbalance in employment relationships.
- **Breach Detection & 72-Hour Notification Process (Art. 33 & Art. 34)** — documented detection, severity classification, controller notification without undue delay (Art. 33(2)), supervisory authority reporting within 72 hours, and internal breach register.
- **Vendor DPA & Sub-processor Register (Art. 28)** + **Legitimate Interest Assessment (LIA) template** for customer Organizations.

Today, none of these compliance documents exist in the repository.

1. **`docs/compliance/ropa.md` — Record of Processing Activities (Art. 30):**
   - Complete table mapping every processing activity to: role (controller vs processor), data subjects, personal data categories, exact D1 & Organization DO tables/columns, legal basis (Art. 6), recipients/sub-processors, international transfer safeguards, technical/organizational security measures (Art. 32), and retention periods (matching `Policy.ts`).
   - Explicit section documenting why anonymous Submissions (`submission`, `answer`) are non-personal data under Recital 26 (citing ADR 0005, ADR 0009, and the `*.privacy.test.ts` invariants).
2. **`docs/compliance/dpia.md` — Data Protection Impact Assessment (Art. 35):**
   - Necessity & proportionality assessment of recurring Team Pulses.
   - Risk register & mitigations:
     - Re-identification of employee feedback → mitigated by ADR 0004 (Minimum group size), ADR 0005 (no Person/time on Submission, zero-observability `SubmissionWorker`), ADR 0009 (store-time Redaction), ADR 0003 (admins see no Results).
     - Free-text PII leakage to AI sub-processors → mitigated by ADR 0015 (opt-in off by default, pre-redacted text only, EU-pinned ZDR endpoints, fail-closed).
     - Point-in-time restore threat model → mitigated by operator access controls, 30-day backup expiry, and explicit disclosure (ADR 0005).
   - Residual risk sign-off template and review cadence.
3. **`docs/compliance/breach-response-runbook.md` — Breach Detection & Notification Runbook (Art. 33–34):**
   - Detection channels (Cloudflare Workers/D1/DO alerts, `check:observability`, canary sweep failures, OpenRouter/sub-processor advisories, unauthorized access).
   - Severity classification matrix (Low / Medium / High / Critical) and decision tree for:
     - Notifying affected customer Organizations without undue delay (Art. 33(2), target ≤ 24h).
     - Notifying the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours (Art. 33(1)) when acting as controller.
     - Notifying affected individuals without undue delay for high-risk breaches (Art. 34).
   - Supervisory authority report template (Art. 33(3) mandatory fields) and breach log template (Art. 33(5)).
4. **`docs/compliance/vendor-dpa-register.md` — Sub-processors, DPAs & Customer LIA Template:**
   - Register of executed/required DPAs and SCC/DPF transfer documentation for Cloudflare, OpenRouter, Google Cloud (Vertex EU), and AWS (Bedrock eu-west-1).
   - Reusable Legitimate Interest Assessment (LIA) template (purpose, necessity, balancing test) that customer Organizations can adopt when rolling out SurveyBeat to EU Teams.

## Done when

- All four documents live in `docs/compliance/`, use exact `GLOSSARY.md` terms, and match the live schemas in `packages/cloudflare/migrations/`, `packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations/`, and `docs/adr/`.
- Cross-referenced from `docs/infra.md` (or `AGENTS.md`) so schema/sub-processor changes prompt updating `docs/compliance/ropa.md`.

===== 296 =====
# What is in and out of Release 3, and how does SPEC §8 re-sequence?

Part of #295

## Question

Confirm the exact scope boundaries of Release 3 "Reach and close the loop" and record the re-sequencing of `SPEC.md §8` (moving Channels, Question rotation, Action follow-up Questions, Comment theme deep-dives, and the remote MCP server ahead of the enterprise Organizations release). Decide whether any small-Team companions (e.g., Live Redaction Preview on the answer page, or R1/R2 deferrals) come along or stay out.

## Output

An R3 scope list that later grilling/research tickets build against, plus the updated `SPEC.md §8` release order.

## Decided in review (2026-11-20)

- **Drop "Live Redaction Preview".** It is not defined in SPEC, GLOSSARY or any ADR. Showing a member their redacted comment before they submit would need a model call from the answer page, which breaks its size budget and adds a new data flow.
- **Release order:** Release 3 = Reach and close the loop. Release 4 = Enterprise Organizations. Release 5 = Public API, webhooks, "Ask your results" and issue-tracker sync. `SPEC.md §8` records this order.
- **Slack and Microsoft Teams both ship in Release 3.** Slack is sliced first (SPEC §10 Q5's default) and Teams follows on the same `ChannelSender` port. Update SPEC §10 Q5 to match.
- **Stale release references:** add a one-line note to ADR 0002 ("Deferred to Release 3 with SSO") and ADR 0003 ("leadership roll-ups (Release 3)") that points to the re-sequencing, so neither is rewritten silently.

===== 297 =====
# Can vercel/chat run on Cloudflare Workers with Alchemy and Effect 4 for Slack and Microsoft Teams?

Part of #295

## Question

Evaluate `vercel/chat` (`chat`, `@chat-adapter/slack`, `@chat-adapter/teams`) inside SurveyBeat's Cloudflare Workers + Alchemy + Effect 4.1.x toolchain (`nodejs_compat`, `packages/cloudflare`). Compare it against thin custom Effect adapters for Slack and Microsoft Teams.

Check specifically:
- Workerd compatibility and bundle footprint for Slack and Teams adapters.
- Webhook signature verification and stateless request handling in `MainWorker`.
- Whether a Durable Object SQLite `StateAdapter` is needed for our outbound-first + slash-command surface.
- Card rendering fidelity (Slack Block Kit and Teams Adaptive Cards) for Invitation cards with 1-tap Answer links, Reminders, and Shared Results summaries.
- Slack app and Microsoft Teams bot/app registration & OAuth installation requirements per Organization.

## Output

A written research note recommending `vercel/chat` or thin custom adapters, with concrete constraints for the Channel delivery ADR.

## Also check (added in review, 2026-11-20)

- **State storage:** does `vercel/chat` need Redis or another external store for state? A third-party store would break the Cloudflare-only rule (SPEC §6), so the answer decides whether a Durable Object SQLite `StateAdapter` is required.
- **Teams proactive messages:** what sending an Invitation unprompted needs, such as an Azure Bot registration and a stored conversation reference per user, and where that reference lives (D1 or the Organization Durable Object).
- **Microsoft Teams Safe Links:** test whether Safe Links keeps the URL fragment `#t=…&v=…` on a link to `answer.html`. If it does not, Teams Invitations offer "Open check-in" only.
- **Slack interaction events:** confirm that plain message links (no Block Kit buttons) send no `block_actions` or other event to our request URL when clicked.

===== 301 =====
# How should the remote MCP server authenticate and serve Streamable HTTP on MainWorker?

Part of #295

## Question

Evaluate the authentication and transport stack for SurveyBeat's remote Streamable HTTP MCP server (`/mcp`) on `MainWorker`:
- Compare Better Auth's `@better-auth/mcp` plugin (OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + consent screen over SurveyBeat's existing Better Auth 1.7.25 on D1, ADR 0022/0024) against `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider`.
- Evaluate MCP server libraries compatible with Cloudflare Workers and Effect 4.1.x (stateless per-request handler, Effect Schema tool input/output validation, `nodejs_compat`).
- Confirm how an authenticated OAuth token resolves to a SurveyBeat `Person`, active Organization, and `Actor` roles—including immediate revocation when a Person is removed or banned (ADR 0023, ADR 0024).

## Output

A written research note recommending the OAuth + MCP transport stack and D1/DO storage changes.

## Notes from review (2026-11-20)

- ADR 0023 removed ADR 0010's `revoked_session` deny list: revocation is deleting the session row. The MCP token path needs its own equivalent, so a revoked or deleted grant fails the next request.
- **Check that the Person is active and not banned** on every MCP request. ADR 0024 says Better Auth enforces `banned` only on its own endpoints, and a long-lived OAuth token deserves the stricter check.
- Confirm the real package name of Better Auth's MCP / OAuth provider support (as far as we know, the `mcp` plugin in `better-auth/plugins` or `@better-auth/oauth-provider`) at the 1.7.25 pin.

===== 306 =====
# GDPR: Right of Access and Portability — personal data export (Art. 15, Art. 20)

## Why

GDPR Article 15 (Right of Access) and Article 20 (Right to Data Portability) entitle any Person to obtain a copy of all personal data held about them in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format within one month. `SPEC.md` §5.3 requires: *"A person can export and delete their personal data. Anonymous submissions are not personal data under this design, so they survive deletion."*

Today, SurveyBeat has no API endpoint or UI to export a Person's personal data.

## Scope

1. **Domain & API contract (`packages/domain`, `packages/api`):**
   - Add an authenticated self-service endpoint (e.g., `GET /api/me/data-export`) returning a downloadable, versioned JSON document (`Content-Disposition: attachment`).
   - Classify the endpoint in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts` as `NoResultData` (it returns only the caller's own personal records, never another Person's data, never Team Results, and never anonymous Submissions).
2. **Data aggregation across all stores (`packages/cloudflare`):**
   - **D1 auth & global index:** `auth_user` (id, name, email, emailVerified, createdAt, updatedAt), active `auth_session` metadata (no raw session token), `auth_account` provider links (no tokens/secrets), `auth_passkey` metadata (name, deviceType, createdAt — no credential material), `person_index` entries, `organization_claim` rows.
   - **Every Organization Durable Object the human belongs to:**
     - `person` (id, email, time_zone, locale, detected_locale, organization_admin, removed_at)
     - `membership` (Team name/id, role, started_at, ended_at)
     - `participation` (Round id/date, Pulse name — fact of participating, with no Answers)
     - `round_member` (eligible Rounds, send_at, time_zone)
     - `invitation` (status, resend_count, created_at, updated_at — never raw token or hash)
     - `pulse_reminder_opt_out` (Pulse reminder preferences)
     - `action` (Actions where `owner_id` is this Person)
     - `email_send` (emails sent to this Person's email: id, kind, status, timestamps — excluding any raw Invitation token)
     - `test_send` (recent test sends for this Person)
   - **Art. 15(1) transparency metadata embedded in the export:** export timestamp, schema version, processing purposes, legal bases, retention periods, sub-processors, and an explicit note that anonymous Submissions are unlinkable non-personal data (ADR 0005) and that browser-local kept answers can be viewed or cleared on `/history` (ADR 0017).
3. **Web UI (`apps/web`):**
   - Add a "Download my personal data" action in the account / privacy area (accessible to every signed-in Person, including non-admins and people in `NotInOrganization` state if they still hold a D1 `auth_user` row).
4. **Tests:**
   - Unit and adapter tests proving complete personal data inclusion across D1 + multiple Organizations.
   - Privacy test (`*.privacy.test.ts`) proving:
     - Caller A can never export Person B's data.
     - No anonymous `submission` or `answer` rows, no raw Invitation tokens, no Edit key hashes, and no Team Results ever appear in the export.

## Done when

- Any signed-in human can download a complete, machine-readable JSON export of their personal data from D1 and all linked Organization Durable Objects.
- `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts`, `registry.privacy.test.ts`, and a new export privacy test pass.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm test:privacy` pass.
===== 307 =====
# GDPR: Right to Erasure — true personal data deletion for People (Art. 17)

## Why

GDPR Article 17 (Right to Erasure) and `SPEC.md` §5.3 require that a Person can have their personal data deleted without undue delay (within 30 days).

# GDPR: Right to Rectification, Restriction, and Objection (Art. 16, Art. 18, Art. 21)

## Why

Beyond Access (Art. 15), Portability (Art. 20), and Erasure (Art. 17), GDPR grants data subjects three additional rights that must be exercisable within one month:
- **Right to Rectification (Art. 16):** Correct inaccurate personal data. Today, a Person can update their language (`directory.updateOwnLanguage`) and delivery time zone (`/delivery`), but **neither a Person nor an Organization admin can update a Person's email address** (e.g. fixing a typo or updating after a legal name change) without removing and re-adding them and losing their Memberships/Actions.
- **Right to Object (Art. 21):** In EU workplace settings, employee consent is rarely "freely given" (Recital 43), so Organizations typically rely on Art. 6(1)(f) Legitimate Interest for Pulse check-ins — which triggers an unconditional right to object. Today, `/unsubscribe` (`pulse_reminder_opt_out`) only suppresses **reminders** for one Pulse; a Person has no way to opt out of Pulse invitations themselves.
- **Right to Restriction of Processing (Art. 18):** When a Person contests accuracy or objects pending verification, their data may be stored but must not be actively processed (no invitations, reminders, or outbound emails).

## Scope

1. **Right to Rectification (Art. 16) — Email address update:**
   - **Self-service:** Signed-in Person verifies a new email address via Better Auth email OTP and propagates the normalized email atomically to `auth_user.email`, `person_index.email`, and `person.email` in every linked Organization Durable Object (rejecting collisions cleanly).
   - **Admin-assisted (for unlinked Persons):** Allow an Organization admin to correct the email address of a Person who has not yet signed in (`auth_user_id IS NULL`), updating `person.email` and `person_index.email`.
2. **Right to Object (Art. 21) — Pulse invitation opt-out:**
   - Extend opt-out beyond reminders (`pulse_reminder_opt_out`) so a Person can opt out of receiving **all Pulse invitations** for a specific Pulse or across the entire Organization, both from an authenticated preferences screen and from the email preference page (`/unsubscribe`).
   - Update Round opening (`packages/cloudflare/src/organization/RoundJobs.ts`) to exclude opted-out People from `round_member` / `invitation` generation (and reflect opted-out count safely without exposing who opted out if that would break privacy, or treat as ineligible for that Round).
3. **Right to Restriction of Processing (Art. 18):**
   - Add a `processing_restricted_at` (nullable timestamp) field on `person` (new DO migration, locked in `migrations.lock.json`).
   - While restricted: the Person receives no Invitations, Reminders, or Results-ready emails, and cannot be added to new Pulses/Teams, while their account/Membership record remains stored for legal/dispute resolution until lifted or erased.
   - Expose restriction toggle to Organization admins (to fulfill Art. 18 requests) and show status to the Person.
4. **Tests:**
   - Domain + SQL + privacy tests covering email rectification across D1 and DO, invitation opt-out exclusion during Round open, and restriction enforcement.

## Done when

- People can rectify their verified email, object to Pulse invitations, and have processing restricted on request.
- All new endpoints are registered in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts`.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm test:privacy` pass.

# GDPR: Automated data retention and storage limitation enforcement (Art. 5(1)(e))

## Why

GDPR Article 5(1)(e) (Storage Limitation) prohibits retaining personal data longer than necessary for its stated purpose. `SPEC.md` §5.3 also explicitly requires: *"An organization sets a retention period for raw answers and comments, defaulting to 24 months. Aggregated results can be kept longer."*

Today, apart from `test_send` / `test_invitation_index` (7-day cleanup), **no table in D1 or the Organization Durable Object enforces any retention limit**:
- Raw `submission` and `answer` rows (including comments) and D1 `submission_index` rows live forever; `organization` has no retention-period setting.
- `email_send` in the Organization DO keeps plaintext `recipient` email addresses and message `content` forever.
- `email_message` and non-production `captured_email` in D1 grow indefinitely.
- Expired `auth_session` (which contain `ipAddress` and `userAgent`) and expired `auth_verification` OTP/magic-link rows in D1 are never purged.
- Closed-Round `invitation`, `invitation_index`, and `round_member` rows persist forever even though the Round is closed.
- Soft-removed `person` rows (`removed_at IS NOT NULL`) retain plaintext `email` indefinitely.

## Scope

1. **Configurable Organization retention for raw Answers & comments (`SPEC.md` §5.3):**
   - Add `raw_answer_retention_months` column on `organization` (new DO migration, default `24`, valid range e.g. `1`–`60` months; exposed in Organization settings API and UI).
   - Enforce automatically via the Organization DO scheduled maintenance/alarm job:
     - Select Rounds where `closed_at <= cutoff` (keying strictly off `round.closed_at` rather than adding any timestamp to `submission`, preserving ADR 0005).
     - Delete `submission` rows (cascading to `answer`) and clean up matching `submission_index` rows in D1.
     - Keep `round_result` (aggregated scores) and `round_themes` intact.
2. **Bounded retention sweeps for operational PII:**
   - **`email_send` (DO):** Scrub `recipient` and `content` (or delete settled rows) after a fixed operational window (e.g. 90 days; define constant in `packages/domain/src/Policy.ts`).
   - **`invitation` & `round_member` (DO) + `invitation_index` (D1):** Purge closed/cancelled Round invitation tokens and `invitation_index` routing rows after a bounded grace window (e.g. 30 days after Round close).
   - **Soft-removed `person` rows (DO):** Automatically scrub residual PII on `person` rows whose `removed_at` exceeds the configured grace period (or align with Art. 17 erasure).
   - **D1 daily cron sweep (`packages/cloudflare/src/MainWorker.ts`):**
     - Delete expired `auth_session` (cascading to `auth_session_organization`) and expired `auth_verification` rows.
     - Delete old `email_message` rows past the delivery-event window (e.g. 30 days).
     - On non-production stages, purge `captured_email` rows older than 7 days.
3. **Retention execution log:**
   - Record non-PII retention run metadata (category, cutoff timestamp, rows purged, run timestamp) so storage-limitation compliance is demonstrable under Art. 5(2).
4. **Tests:**
   - Unit and SQLite tests verifying each cutoff boundary (including that aggregated `round_result` survives raw Answer purge and that `submission` still carries no timestamp per ADR 0005).

## Done when

- Organization admins can configure raw Answer/comment retention (default 24 months) in Settings.
- Scheduled DO and D1 retention jobs automatically purge expired PII and raw Answers/comments without touching aggregated Results.
- Every retention period is defined in `Policy.ts` and matches the public Privacy Notice.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm test:privacy` pass.

# GDPR: Data minimization and EU data residency hardening (Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 25, Art. 44–49)

## Why

GDPR Article 5(1)(c) requires collecting only the minimum personal data strictly needed, Article 25 mandates privacy by design and default, and Articles 44–49 govern transfers of personal data outside the EEA.

An audit of the current codebase found three concrete hardening gaps:

1. **Invitation tokens appear in URL query strings on `MainWorker`:**
   - `packages/cloudflare/src/PageRoutes.ts` and `ServerPages.ts` accept `?token=...` on `GET /delivery` and `?t=...` on `GET /unsubscribe` on `MainWorker`.
   - Unlike `SubmissionWorker`, `MainWorker` has Workers Logs enabled (1% sampling), and query strings also leak into browser history and `Referer` headers. Reusing the Invitation token in query strings weakens token isolation and exposes a personal identifier (`invitation_index` maps `token_hash -> person_id`) in server logs.
2. **Unused PII captured in Better Auth sessions and plugin tables:**
   - `packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations/0008_better_auth.sql` stores `ipAddress` and `userAgent` on every `auth_session` row, even though no SurveyBeat feature uses them.
   - `MainWorker.ts` forwards all unmatched `/auth/*` paths directly to Better Auth, exposing plugin routes (`organization`, `admin` per ADR 0024) backed by unused tables (`auth_organization`, `auth_member`, `auth_invitation`) that are not part of SurveyBeat's tenant model.
3. **No EU data residency configuration on D1 or Organization Durable Objects:**
   - ADR 0015 pins AI processing strictly to EU endpoints (`google-vertex/europe`, `amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1`), yet `packages/cloudflare/src/Database.ts` (D1) and `packages/cloudflare/src/Organization.ts` (Durable Object) do not configure Cloudflare's EU jurisdiction (`jurisdiction: "eu"` / `locationHint: "weur"`), leaving data-at-rest placement unspecified.

## Scope

1. **Decouple `/delivery` and `/unsubscribe` from Invitation tokens in query strings:**
   - Issue separate, scoped preference tokens (non-redeemable on `SubmissionWorker`) or deliver the token via URL fragment + client POST / signed RFC 8058 POST-only `List-Unsubscribe`, and add `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` headers on those routes.
   - Ensure `MainWorker` never receives a live Invitation token in any URL query string; pin with a privacy test.
2. **Minimize Better Auth PII & surface:**
   - Configure Better Auth (or a database hook in `packages/auth/src/options.ts`) to avoid persisting `ipAddress` and `userAgent` in `auth_session` (or null them at write time) unless required for a documented security control with short retention.
   - Audit `/auth/*` pass-through in `MainWorker.ts` and document/restrict any unused Better Auth plugin endpoints so no unmonitored PII can be written to `auth_organization`, `auth_member`, or `auth_invitation` outside SurveyBeat's DSAR/erasure scope (add an ADR if modifying ADR 0024).
3. **EU data residency for D1 and Organization Durable Objects:**
   - Evaluate Cloudflare `jurisdiction: "eu"` support in `@alchemy.run/cloudflare` for D1 (`Database.ts`) and Durable Objects (`Organization.ts`).
   - Record the decision and any production migration/transfer implications (SCCs / DPF for edge routing) in a new ADR under `docs/adr/`, and apply the configuration to `Database.ts` / `Organization.ts` where supported.

## Done when

- No Invitation token ever travels in a URL query string to `MainWorker`.
- `auth_session` no longer stores unnecessary raw `ipAddress` / `userAgent` PII (or stores only documented, retention-bounded values), and unused Better Auth plugin write surfaces are locked down or covered by DSAR/erasure.
- EU data residency for D1 and Durable Objects is configured and recorded in an ADR.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm test:privacy` pass.

# GDPR: Accountability — privacy & admin audit log and consent/opt-in records (Art. 5(2), Art. 7, Art. 32)

## Why

GDPR Article 5(2) (Accountability) requires controllers and processors to *demonstrate* compliance, Article 7(1) requires provable records of opt-ins/consent (who, when, what version), and Article 32 requires appropriate security monitoring. `SPEC.md` §5.6 also specifies: *"Audit log. The system records admin and lead actions, such as changing privacy settings, changing anonymity modes, exporting data, and adding leads, in a store inside SurveyBeat."*

Today:
- Toggling `organization.ai_processing` (ADR 0015) flips a bare `0`/`1` integer with no record of *which* Organization admin enabled it, *when*, or *under which sub-processor/DPA notice version*.
- Creating an Organization does not record Terms/DPA acceptance timestamp, actor, or document version.
- Admin and privacy-critical actions (changing `minimum_group_size`, changing retention settings, adding/removing/erasing People, granting/revoking admin or Lead roles, exporting data) leave no structured audit trail.

## Scope

1. **Append-only Organization audit log (`packages/cloudflare/migrations/` + `packages/domain`):**
   - Add an `audit_log` table inside each Organization Durable Object (new numbered migration locked in `migrations.lock.json`): `id`, `occurred_at`, `actor_person_id` (nullable for system/retention jobs), `action`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `metadata_json` (strictly typed, schema-validated non-sensitive metadata — e.g., `policyVersion`, old/new `minimumGroupSize`, `aiProcessing` boolean, retention months).
   - **Strict privacy invariant:** `audit_log` must NEVER store Answers, comments, raw Invitation tokens, Edit keys, or anything that could join a Participation record to a Submission (ADR 0005).
2. **Events recorded atomically in the same DO transaction as the state change:**
   - Organization created + Terms/DPA acceptance (`dpaVersion`, `termsVersion`, actor, timestamp).

   - Role changes (`grantAdmin`, `revokeAdmin`, `assignLead`, `removeLead`).
   - People lifecycle (`addMember`, `removeMember`, `removePerson`, Art. 16 email rectification, Art. 18 restriction toggled, Art. 17 erasure executed, Art. 21 invitation opt-out).
   - Data access & retention (`personal_data_exported`, `retention_purge_executed`).
3. **Audit log viewer & retention:**
   - Add an Organization-admin-only `GET /api/organization/audit-log` endpoint (classified as `NoResultData` in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts`) and read-only table in Organization settings.
   - Preserve ADR 0003: Organization admins see governance/privacy events, never Team Results, comments, or participation details.
   - Define audit log retention period in `Policy.ts` (e.g., 24 months) and scrub `actor_person_id` email display cleanly when a Person is erased.
4. **Tests:**
   - Unit and SQLite tests verifying every sensitive command writes an audit entry atomically.
   - Privacy test (`*.privacy.test.ts`) verifying `audit_log` contains zero Answer/comment/token/Result data and cannot be read by non-admins.

## Done when

- Every privacy setting change, AI opt-in, DPA acceptance, role change, and DSAR action produces an immutable, timestamped audit record inside the Organization Durable Object.
- Organization admins can inspect the audit log in Settings without seeing any Team Results.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, and `pnpm test:privacy` pass.
