| `auth_oauth_client` | Registered MCP clients (CIMD/DCR/static) | `clientId` (unique), `redirectUris`, `scopes`, `tokenEndpointAuthMethod`, `requirePKCE`, `disabled`, `userId` |
| `auth_oauth_resource` | Canonical resource policies (`/mcp`) | `identifier` (unique), `allowedScopes`, `accessTokenTtl`, `refreshTokenTtl`, `disabled` |
| `auth_oauth_client_resource` | Client-to-resource allow mapping | `(clientId, resourceId)` unique pair with `ON DELETE CASCADE` |
| `auth_oauth_consent` | Active user-per-Organization grants | `(clientId, userId, referenceId)` where `referenceId` stores SurveyBeat `OrganizationId`; deleting this row revokes the grant |
| `auth_oauth_refresh_token` | Hashed refresh tokens (`offline_access`) | `token` (unique), `clientId`, `userId`, `sessionId` (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), `referenceId`, `scopes`, `resources`, `revoked`, `expiresAt` |
| `auth_oauth_access_token` | Hashed opaque access tokens | `token` (unique), `clientId`, `userId`, `sessionId` (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), `referenceId`, `refreshId`, `scopes`, `resources`, `revoked`, `expiresAt` |
| `auth_oauth_client_assertion` | Optional `private_key_jwt` `jti` replay guard | Only needed if CIMD `private_key_jwt` clients are enabled (`id`, `expiresAt`) |

Note on D1 batching: `@effect/sql-d1` / Cloudflare D1 has no SQL `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` transactions (`docs/research/effect-on-workers.md`), so multi-table grant deletion uses `database.batch([...])`.

### Organization Durable Object

**Zero schema changes required.** The `Organization` DO remains the sole system of record for `person` (`auth_user_id`, `removed_at`, `organization_admin`), `membership` (`team_id`, `person_id`, `role`, `ended_at`), and all survey entities.

### Worker Configuration & Routing

- Add `"/mcp"` and `"/.well-known/*"` to `mainWorkerAssets.runWorkerFirst` in `packages/cloudflare/src/WorkerWiring.ts` and route them in `packages/cloudflare/src/MainWorker.ts` (`/.well-known/*` to `authInstance.fetch`, `/mcp` to the authenticated MCP handler).
- If `@better-auth/cimd` is enabled to fetch external client metadata URLs from `MainWorker`, ensure the `global_fetch_strictly_public` compatibility flag is configured in Alchemy for `MainWorker` (matching Cloudflare's CIMD SSRF guidance).

---

## 6. What Could Not Be Verified

1. **Runtime behavior & bundle size in `workerd`**: No dependencies were installed into `packages/*` and no code was built or deployed; `MainWorker` startup CPU and bundle size with `@better-auth/mcp`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider`, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, and `@cfworker/json-schema` were not measured in local `workerd` or a preview stage.
2. **Exact D1 DDL generated by Better Auth 1.7.25**: Table definitions were read from `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25`'s `oauth-kpy9mh0t.d.mts`, not emitted via Better Auth's SQLite migration generator and exercised against `D1Auth.test.ts`. The Organization admin role (WorkOS's org-level `admin`) covers administration only: Teams, Leads, and People. Seeing a Team's Results, comments, or Actions requires a Membership in that Team, whatever the person's Organization role. Admins are often the people members worry about most. If the admin role could read every Team's Results, it would undercut "trust before features" and put leadership roll-ups (Release 3) in through a side door.

> Extended by ADR 0014 (an Organization admin may add themselves to a Team).
> Note (2026-11-20, #296): Enterprise Organizations (including leadership roll-ups) moved to Release 4 in SPEC §8.

110→## 5. Functional requirements

Requirements are grouped by the loop step they serve. Section 8 sequences them into releases.

### 5.1 Ask: set up and send pulses

- A lead can create a pulse in under two minutes by starting from a template. The product ships with templates for weekly team health, sprint retrospectives, onboarding check-ins (at 30, 60, and 90 days), and a manager feedback round.
- Question types are rating (1 to 5, with labeled ends), eNPS (0 to 10), single choice, multiple choice, short text, and long text. Each rating question can have an optional "Want to say more?" comment field.
- The question library is shared across the organization. Admins can mark questions as standard, so that every team asking the same question produces comparable data across the organization.
- The pulse editor shows an estimated answer time, and warns when a pulse goes over 7 questions or about 90 seconds.
120→- Optional rotation. A pulse can have a fixed core set of questions plus a rotating set, where each round asks one or two different questions. This covers more topics without making each round longer.
- Cadence uses each member's local time zone. Monday 9:00 means 9:00 for each recipient. A lead can skip a round (for holidays) or pause a pulse.
- Channels are email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams. Each member picks their preferred channel. Email is the fallback for everyone.
- The first question can be answered directly from the message. In email, each rating value is a link that opens the answer page with that value chosen; the answer is saved when the member confirms it there, because email security scanners open every link (ADR 0007). In Slack and Teams, the message has interactive buttons and, where the platform allows it, a modal for the rest.
- Reminders go only to members who have not answered, and there are at most two per round. A member can turn reminders off.
- A shareable link remains available for teams that do not use invitations. A link round cannot compute a response rate and cannot guarantee one answer per person. The UI says so.

### 5.2 Answer: the member experience

- The answer page loads in under one second on a mid-range phone on 4G. It needs no sign-in when opened from an invitation token. It does need sign-in when opened from the shared link, if the organization requires it.

245→
Each release is usable on its own. Ship a release to a real team (your own, first) before starting the next.

**Release 1. The core loop for one team.**
Sign-in with an email code, plus organization and team setup by hand. Pulses from templates, with rating, choice, and text questions. Weekly cadence with time zones. Email invitations with one-tap first answers, and reminders. Anonymous mode with the minimum group size. Round results with trends and sample sizes. Actions with owner and status, shown in the next invitation. The full privacy test suite. Preview environments per pull request.
250→
**Release 2. Insight.**
Comment redaction and themes. Discussion guide. Team health overview with action markers. Delayed sharing. The member's private history page. German translation, deferred: English only for now (ADR 0025).

**Release 3. Reach and close the loop.**
Channel-agnostic delivery across Email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams. Slack ships first; Microsoft Teams follows on the same port. Core and Rotating Questions. One-Round Questions for Action follow-ups and Comment theme deep-dives. A privacy-enforced remote MCP server.

**Release 4. Enterprise Organizations.**
Enterprise SSO and Directory Sync. Nested teams and leadership roll-ups with subtraction-safe thresholds. Standard questions and cross-team comparison. Confidential mode. Audit log. Exports.

260→**Release 5. Open up.**
Public API and webhooks. "Ask your results". Issue tracker sync for actions.

## 9. Out of scope

- Individual performance reviews, 360 reviews, and anything that scores a single person. Those features change what members believe the tool is for, and they would erode trust in anonymous team health data.
- A general-purpose form builder. SurveyBeat asks short, recurring questions. Leads who need branching logic, file uploads, or 40-question forms should use a form tool.
- Industry benchmarks against other companies' data. Revisit this only when there is enough data and a legal basis to pool it.
- Native mobile apps. Email, chat, and a fast mobile web page cover the need.

Prefix every agent-authored comment left on the user's behalf with this GitHub
note callout:

20→
If the harness does not expose a model name, use the harness name. Do not guess.

Before posting, check the entire comment, including quoted text and
attachments, for secrets and private details.

Keep the attribution inside the note and the actual reply outside it. The
context line must start with the robot emoji. Do not add a horizontal rule,
Setext underline, heading, signature footer, or a second attribution.

30→Apply this format to top-level PR comments, inline review comments, replies to
bots or reviewers, and written explanations used before resolving or
dismissing feedback. Do not add it to PR descriptions, commit messages, or text
the user explicitly asked to post verbatim without attribution.

Write the comment itself in a direct style:

- Lead with the conclusion.
- Cite the relevant code, behavior, check, or reproduction.
- Keep it concise and avoid filler, canned thanks, or status narration.
40→- Distinguish verified facts from judgment.

Preview the final Markdown before posting so quoting and blank lines render as
shown. After posting, verify that GitHub returned the comment or review URL.
Resolve a review thread only after its response was posted successfully.

content.text: The security constraints are legitimate for a research note proposing an auth design.

70→5. Enforce `Origin` validation on `/mcp` (matching `trustedOrigins` or absent `Origin` for non-browser CLI/desktop clients) against DNS rebinding, and register every MCP tool's domain read/write in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts` (or a sibling MCP privacy check) per SPEC §7.

---

## 4. Token-to-Actor Resolution, Revocation, and Active/Banned Checks

SurveyBeat's domain model separates the global auth user (`AuthUserId` = `auth_user.id`) from per-Organization tenancy (`OrganizationId` + `PersonId` + `Actor`). One human may be different `Person`s across multiple Organizations (`D1PeopleIndex`, ADR 0022/0023).

```text
Bearer Token ──▶ [D1 Auth Check on MainWorker]
80→                    ├─ Hash token ─▶ auth_oauth_access_token (active, unrevoked, unexpired)
                    ├─ Grant check ─▶ auth_oauth_consent exists for (clientId, userId, referenceId)
                    ├─ Client check ─▶ auth_oauth_client.disabled = 0
                    ├─ Session check ─▶ if sessionId != null, auth_session exists & unexpired
                    └─ Ban check ────▶ auth_user.banned = 0 (or expired banExpires)
                          │
                          ▼ yields (authUserId, organizationId = referenceId, scopes)
                 [Organization Durable Object RPC]
                    ├─ person row: auth_user_id = authUserId AND removed_at IS NULL
                    ├─ membership rows: ended_at IS NULL
90→                    └─ actorOf(directoryState, person.id) ─▶ Actor { personId, organizationAdmin, roles }
```

### Step-by-Step Resolution

1. **Consent-time Organization binding (`postLogin.consentReferenceId`)**:
   - During `/auth/oauth2/authorize`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider` runs `postLogin` after browser sign-in and before consent.
   - Using `D1PeopleIndex.linkedPersons(authUserId)` (and **not** Better Auth's `auth_organization` / `auth_member` tables, per ADR 0024), resolve the human's linked Organizations:
     - **Zero linked active Persons**: deny authorization (the human has no Organization membership to grant).
     - **One linked Organization**: `postLogin` passes automatically and `consentReferenceId` returns that `OrganizationId`.
100→     - **Multiple linked Organizations**: `postLogin` redirects to a SurveyBeat Organization-selection page (reusing the candidate-picker semantics from `SignInFlow.ts`), records the selected `OrganizationId` for the authorize continuation, and `consentReferenceId` returns it.
   - Better Auth persists that `OrganizationId` in `referenceId` on `auth_oauth_consent`, `auth_oauth_refresh_token`, and `auth_oauth_access_token`. Pinning each OAuth grant to one `OrganizationId` prevents an MCP client token from crossing Organizations or shifting silently when the human switches Organizations in the web app (`auth_session_organization`).
2. **Per-request D1 verification on `MainWorker` (auth plane)**:
   - Extract `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (reject missing/malformed tokens with `401` and RFC 9728 `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="..."`).
   - Compute the stored token digest matching Better Auth's `storeTokens` hash and execute a single D1 lookup joining `auth_oauth_access_token`, `auth_oauth_client`, `auth_oauth_consent`, `auth_user`, and (left join) `auth_session`:
     - Token row exists, `revoked IS NULL`, and `expiresAt > now`.
     - `auth_oauth_client` exists and `disabled = 0`.
     - **`auth_oauth_consent` row exists** matching `(clientId, userId, referenceId)` and covers the token's scopes/resources.

   - Call the `Organization` Durable Object identified by `organizationId` (`referenceId`) to resolve the active `Person` and `Actor` (`organizationDirectory.activePerson(authUserId)` / `actorOf(directoryState, personId)` in `packages/domain/src/people/Directory.ts`).
   - The DO checks `person.auth_user_id = authUserId AND person.removed_at IS NULL` and computes `Actor { personId, organizationAdmin, roles }` from active `membership` rows (`ended_at IS NULL`).
   - If the `Person` was removed (`removed_at IS NOT NULL`) or deactivated, `activePerson` / `actorOf` returns `None`, and `/mcp` immediately fails the request (`401` / `403`).
   - Every MCP tool passes `Actor` (or `actorId` + DO enforcement) through the existing domain permission function `can(actor, action, resource)` and privacy rules (minimum group size, subtraction-safe roll-ups, comment redaction, Lead-only discussion guides, review windows).

### Revocation Semantics (ADR 0023)

- **No deny list**: Consistent with ADR 0023 (which deleted `revoked_session`), revocation deletes the grant/token rows directly in D1; no deny-list table is added.
- **Immediate failure on next request**:
  - **User revokes an MCP client grant** (from SurveyBeat settings or `/oauth2/delete-consent`): delete the `auth_oauth_consent` row **and** delete matching `auth_oauth_access_token` and `auth_oauth_refresh_token` rows in one `database.batch([...])` call. Because the `/mcp` verifier requires both the `auth_oauth_access_token` row and the `auth_oauth_consent` row, the very next `/mcp` request fails with `401 invalid_token`.
  - **OAuth client calls `/oauth2/revoke`**: `revokeOpaqueAccessToken` deletes the `auth_oauth_access_token` row immediately; `revokeRefreshToken` marks `revoked` on `auth_oauth_refresh_token` and deletes linked `auth_oauth_access_token` rows.
  - **Admin bans a user (`banUser`) or removes a Person (`RemovePerson`)**: `auth_user.banned = 1` and `person.removed_at != NULL` both fail the very next `/mcp` request immediately, and the workflow should also delete matching `auth_oauth_consent`, `auth_oauth_access_token`, and `auth_oauth_refresh_token` rows in D1 (`userId` / `(userId, referenceId)`) so no stale refresh grant lingers.

---

## 5. Storage Changes

### D1 (`packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations/0011_better_auth_mcp.sql` + `d1-migrations.lock.json`)

D1 remains strictly the global auth/routing index—**no survey content** (no Pulses, Rounds, Submissions, Answers, Results, Themes, Actions, or Notes) is ever stored in D1.

With `disableJwtPlugin: true`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` needs six `auth_`-prefixed tables (mapped in `AUTH_TABLES` in `packages/auth/src/options.ts`, no `jwks` table needed):

| Table | Purpose | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auth_oauth_client` | Registered MCP clients (CIMD/DCR/static) | `clientId` (unique), `redirectUris`, `scopes`, `tokenEndpointAuthMethod`, `requirePKCE`, `disabled`, `userId` |
| `auth_oauth_resource` | Canonical resource policies (`/mcp`) | `identifier` (unique), `allowedScopes`, `accessTokenTtl`, `refreshTokenTtl`, `disabled` |
| `auth_oauth_client_resource` | Client-to-resource allow mapping | `(clientId, resourceId)` unique pair with `ON DELETE CASCADE` |
| `auth_oauth_consent` | Active user-per-Organization grants | `(clientId, userId, referenceId)` where `referenceId` stores SurveyBeat `OrganizationId`; deleting this row revokes the grant |
| `auth_oauth_refresh_token` | Hashed refresh tokens (`offline_access`) | `token` (unique), `clientId`, `userId`, `sessionId` (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), `referenceId`, `scopes`, `resources`, `revoked`, `expiresAt` |
| `auth_oauth_access_token` | Hashed opaque access tokens | `token` (unique), `clientId`, `userId`, `sessionId` (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), `referenceId`, `refreshId`, `scopes`, `resources`, `revoked`, `expiresAt` |
| `auth_oauth_client_assertion` | Optional `private_key_jwt` `jti` replay guard | Only needed if CIMD `private_key_jwt` clients are enabled (`id`, `expiresAt`) |

Note on D1 batching: `@effect/sql-d1` / Cloudflare D1 has no SQL `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` transactions (`docs/research/effect-on-workers.md`), so multi-table grant deletion uses `database.batch([...])`.

### Organization Durable Object

**Zero schema changes required.** The `Organization` DO remains the sole system of record for `person` (`auth_user_id`, `removed_at`, `organization_admin`), `membership` (`team_id`, `person_id`, `role`, `ended_at`), and all survey entities.

The delete-consent endpoint only deletes the consent row.

The research note already requires deleting both the consent row and matching tokens in one batch. CodeRabbit flags that Better Auth's stock endpoint only removes the consent row, leaving old tokens intact. A later new consent could then re-validate those surviving tokens.

The implementation must explicitly replace the stock `deleteConsentEndpoint` rather than use it as-is. Tokens should be bound to a grant generation so a later re-grant cannot revive old ones. Next, I will verify DPoP and resource audience claims in `token.ts`.

Verified that `createOpaqueAccessToken` stores the DPoP confirmation on the access token row.

`confirmationTokenType` returns "DPoP" when a `jkt` is present. The research note's Bearer lookup does not check confirmation. The `/mcp` endpoint must reject DPoP-bound tokens unless the request proves the key. Alternatively, SurveyBeat could disable DPoP-bound issuance. The note recommends opaque Bearer tokens.

The clean path is to reject sender-constrained tokens at the verifier and avoid issuing DPoP-bound tokens for `/mcp` in this slice. The research note should record this constraint rather than invent a DPoP implementation. Token `resources` represent audience, not consent covering scopes.

The token's `resources` must include the canonical MCP resource identifier.

`can()` does not see token scopes. A read-only token could still write if the person is an admin.

The stock `/oauth2/delete-consent` endpoint only deletes the consent row. It does not delete tokens. The note incorrectly names this endpoint for batch revocation. The old token would still match a later new consent. Do not rely on the stock endpoint. Replace it or the old token remains valid.

I will update the research note in the worktree and commit. I should check whether the 313 commit is still running tests to avoid colliding with the full pre-commit gate. I will reply to the review threads after pushing the fix.

I will add a `confirmation` column note to the access-token table. The step 2 digest lookup bullets will include a rejection rule for rows with a sender confirmation key, since Better Auth 1.7.25 stores that key on opaque tokens and this slice does not validate DPoP proofs.

The note must explicitly forbid advertising `dpop_bound_access_tokens` for the `/mcp` resource and reject any DPoP-bound token on the Bearer path. Step 3 should require the token's scopes to include the scope mapped to the specific tool, since `can()` cannot see OAuth scopes and a read-only token must still be blocked from write operations.

The comparison table already notes KV revocation is immediate but subject to cross-location consistency. Opus flagged that the cell should clarify it is not immediate across locations.

The worktree already includes the eventual consistency caveat. Opus likely reviewed the committed version at c1b4b943, which may have lacked that parenthetical. I will read the exact lines to verify.

110→     - If the token row's `confirmation` has a DPoP `jkt`, reject the request. `createOpaqueAccessToken` in `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` stores that key, and `confirmationTokenType` presents it as `DPoP`, not `Bearer`. This slice does not validate DPoP proofs or their replay cache. Do not advertise `dpop_bound_access_tokens` for the `/mcp` resource, and do not accept a sender-constrained token on the Bearer path.
     - If `sessionId IS NOT NULL` (or if `offline_access` was not granted), the `auth_session` row still exists and `expiresAt > now`.
     - **`auth_user.banned` check (ADR 0024)**: reject immediately if `banned = 1` and (`banExpires IS NULL` or `banExpires > now`). Also enforce the same `banned` check in `oauthProvider` hooks before `/oauth2/authorize`, `/oauth2/consent`, and `/oauth2/token` (`refresh_token` grant) so banned accounts cannot obtain or refresh tokens.
     - Verify `referenceId` is a non-empty `OrganizationId` (and check optional `person_index` existence).
3. **Per-request Organization DO verification (tenant & `Actor` plane)**:
   - Call the `Organization` Durable Object identified by `organizationId` (`referenceId`) to resolve the active `Person` and `Actor` (`organizationDirectory.activePerson(authUserId)` / `actorOf(directoryState, personId)` in `packages/domain/src/people/Directory.ts`).
   - The DO checks `person.auth_user_id = authUserId AND person.removed_at IS NULL` and computes `Actor { personId, organizationAdmin, roles }` from active `membership` rows (`ended_at IS NULL`).
   - If the `Person` was removed (`removed_at IS NOT NULL`) or deactivated, `activePerson` / `actorOf` returns `None`, and `/mcp` immediately fails the request (`401` / `403`).
   - Every MCP tool passes `Actor` (or `actorId` + DO enforcement) through the existing domain permission function `can(actor, action, resource)` and privacy rules (minimum group size, subtraction-safe roll-ups, comment redaction, Lead-only discussion guides, review windows).
   - The same call also requires the token's stored scopes to include the scope mapped to that tool. `can` in `packages/domain/src/people/Permissions.ts` does not see OAuth scopes. A read-only token must fail a write even when the `Person` is an Organization admin.
120→

- **No deny list**: Consistent with ADR 0023 (which deleted `revoked_session`), revocation deletes the grant/token rows directly in D1; no deny-list table is added.
- **Immediate failure on next request**:
  - **User revokes an MCP client grant**: delete the `auth_oauth_consent` row **and** the matching `auth_oauth_access_token` and `auth_oauth_refresh_token` rows for `(clientId, userId, referenceId)` in one `database.batch([...])` call. The stock `deleteConsentEndpoint` in `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` (`oauthConsent/endpoints.ts`) deletes only the consent row. Do not mount that endpoint unchanged. A later grant for the same client and Organization inserts a new consent row, and an unexpired old token would pass the consent join. Because the `/mcp` verifier requires both the access-token row and the consent row, deleting both makes the next request fail with `401 invalid_token`.
  - **OAuth client calls `/oauth2/revoke`**: `revokeOpaqueAccessToken` deletes the `auth_oauth_access_token` row immediately; `revokeRefreshToken` marks `revoked` on `auth_oauth_refresh_token` and deletes linked `auth_oauth_access_token` rows.
  - **Admin bans a user (`banUser`) or removes a Person (`RemovePerson`)**: `auth_user.banned = 1` and `person.removed_at != NULL` both fail the very next `/mcp` request immediately, and the workflow should also delete matching `auth_oauth_consent`, `auth_oauth_access_token`, and `auth_oauth_refresh_token` rows in D1 (`userId` / `(userId, referenceId)`) so no stale refresh grant lingers.

---
130→

D1 remains strictly the global auth/routing index—**no survey content** (no Pulses, Rounds, Submissions, Answers, Results, Themes, Actions, or Notes) is ever stored in D1.

With `disableJwtPlugin: true`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` needs six `auth_`-prefixed tables (mapped in `AUTH_TABLES` in `packages/auth/src/options.ts`, no `jwks` table needed):

| Table | Purpose | Notes |
140→| --- | --- | --- |
| `auth_oauth_client` | Registered MCP clients (CIMD/DCR/static) | `clientId` (unique), `redirectUris`, `scopes`, `tokenEndpointAuthMethod`, `requirePKCE`, `disabled`, `userId` |
| `auth_oauth_resource` | Canonical resource policies (`/mcp`) | `identifier` (unique), `allowedScopes`, `accessTokenTtl`, `refreshTokenTtl`, `disabled` |
| `auth_oauth_client_resource` | Client-to-resource allow mapping | `(clientId, resourceId)` unique pair with `ON DELETE CASCADE` |
| `auth_oauth_consent` | Active user-per-Organization grants | `(clientId, userId, referenceId)` where `referenceId` stores SurveyBeat `OrganizationId`; deleting this row revokes the grant |

# Leaving PR Comments

Prefix every agent-authored comment left on the user's behalf with this GitHub
note callout:
10→
```md
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **<model> responding on behalf of <user>**

Actual comment starts here.
```

Use the verified public name of the model that wrote the comment, and the
user's name or GitHub login.
20→
If the harness does not expose a model name, use the harness name. Do not guess.

Before posting, check the entire comment, including quoted text and
attachments, for secrets and private details.

Keep the attribution inside the note and the actual reply outside it. The
context line must start with the robot emoji. Do not add a horizontal rule,
Setext underline, heading, signature footer, or a second attribution.

30→Apply this format to top-level PR comments, inline review comments, replies to
bots or reviewers, and written explanations used before resolving or
dismissing feedback. Do not add it to PR descriptions, commit messages, or text
the user explicitly asked to post verbatim without attribution.

Write the comment itself in a direct style:

- Lead with the conclusion.
- Cite the relevant code, behavior, check, or reproduction.
- Keep it concise and avoid filler, canned thanks, or status narration.
40→- Distinguish verified facts from judgment.

Preview the final Markdown before posting so quoting and blank lines render as
shown. After posting, verify that GitHub returned the comment or review URL.
Resolve a review thread only after its response was posted successfully.

name: long-running-background-tasks
description: >-
  Required reading before you start, watch, or wait on anything that keeps running after you launch it — background jobs, watchers, scheduled loops, CI, pull requests, training runs, dev servers, long builds. Read it before you launch such work and before you report on its state. Saying where a running job stands counts as working on it. Use when: about to launch, supervise, inspect, diagnose, or report on work that keeps running after it is started.
---

# Working with long-running background tasks

Only submitting or queuing jobs is not sufficient to complete the task. The definition of done is the job has completed successfully and you have verified that it has produced all the expected outputs.
10→
This means you must see through the jobs completion by watching the job to ensure that its healthy, progressing, and working as intended.

## Tools available

There's two ways to watch jobs: monitor and loop. Decide which of the two you need, sometimes you need both.

### monitor — deterministic, actionable events

- Use a monitor when the event is a predicate a script can evaluate — an API response, an exit code, a port answering.
20→- Typical events: CI turning red, a PR comment or merge conflict, a PR becoming ready to merge, a dev server coming up or going down, a job reaching a terminal state.
- The monitor requires a script polls on a fixed cadence and stays silent until the predicate fires, so an idle job costs nothing. More on writing good monitoring scripts below.
- Examples of when to use:
  - Monitoring a PR — wake on CI breaking, merge conflicts, etc.
  - Checking if local tooling is up — wake on the service being unavailable, errors, etc.

# Working with long-running background tasks

Only submitting or queuing jobs is not sufficient to complete the task. The definition of done is the job has completed successfully and you have verified that it has produced all the expected outputs.

There's two ways to watch jobs: monitor and loop. Decide which of the two you need, sometimes you need both.

- Use a monitor when the event is a predicate a script can evaluate — an API response, an exit code, a port answering.
- Typical events: CI turning red, a PR comment or merge conflict, a PR becoming ready to merge, a dev server coming up or going down, a job reaching a terminal state.

- Examples of when to use:
  - Monitoring a PR — wake on CI breaking, merge conflicts, etc.
  - Checking if local tooling is up — wake on the service being unavailable, errors, etc.
  - All of these wakeup cases can be checked deterministically.

### loop — qualitative health that needs reading

- Use a loop when judging health requires reading the logs and system information to detect failing, faulty or stalled jobs. It uses a subagent which is more expensive but more thorough.
- Typical signals: the loss curve going unstable, a filtering pipeline producing garbage, throughput quietly degrading, faulty nodes throwing CUDA errors.
- A subagent reads the logs on a fixed cadence (say every 10 min) and reports what changed, so it costs a wakeup every cycle.

Default JWT mode is **not** immediately revocable (see traps below). | Immediate via KV revocation/deletion (subject to KV eventual consistency if written and read across colos). |

2. **Deleting consent does not revoke existing tokens**: Better Auth's `/oauth2/delete-consent` (`deleteConsentEndpoint`) deletes the `oauthConsent` row without deleting `oauthAccessToken` or `oauthRefreshToken` rows, and `revokeRefreshToken` marks `revoked = <timestamp>` rather than deleting the row. Moreover, `prepareBackchannelLogoutPlan` intentionally spares `offline_access` refresh tokens when a browser session is deleted, and `oauthAccessToken.sessionId` uses `ON DELETE SET NULL`. Therefore, `/mcp` must verify **both** the token row and an active `oauthConsent` grant row in D1.
- If `sessionId IS NOT NULL` (or if `offline_access` was not granted), the `auth_session` row still exists and `expiresAt > now`.

- If the `Person` was removed (`removed_at IS NOT NULL`) or deactivated, `activePerson` / `actorOf` returns `None`, and `/mcp` immediately fails the request (`401` / `403`).
With `disableJwtPlugin: true`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` needs six `auth_`-prefixed tables (mapped in `AUTH_TABLES` in `packages/auth/src/options.ts`, no `jwks` table needed):

| `auth_oauth_refresh_token` | Hashed refresh tokens (`offline_access`) | `token` (unique), `clientId`, `userId`, `sessionId` (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), `referenceId`, `scopes`, `resources`, `revoked`, `expiresAt` |

### Primary-Source Traps in `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` & `@better-auth/mcp@1.7.25`

Inspecting `authorize-BJStuGWz.mjs` (`@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25`), `index.mjs` (`@better-auth/mcp@1.7.25`), and `verify.mjs` (`@better-auth/core@1.7.25`) revealed four critical traps that shape SurveyBeat's implementation:

1. **Default JWT mode breaks immediate revocation**: In `createUserTokens` (`authorize-BJStuGWz.mjs`), `isJwtAccessToken = REDACTED && !opts.disableJwtPlugin`. Because `mcp({ resource })` always sets `audienceClaim`, it mints stateless JWT access tokens (3600s default TTL) unless `disableJwtPlugin: true` is set. `requireMcpAuth()` validates JWTs locally via JWKS (`verifyAccessTokenRequest`) with **no D1 lookup**, and `/oauth2/revoke` (`revokeJwtAccessToken`) rejects JWT access tokens with `unsupported_token_type`. Setting **`disableJwtPlugin: true`** switches access tokens to opaque tokens stored by hash in `auth_oauth_access_token`, avoids adding a `jwks` table in D1, and makes `/oauth2/revoke` delete the `oauthAccessToken` row. (Note: when `disableJwtPlugin: true`, `storeClientSecret` must remain `"encrypted"`—its default—not `"hashed"`.)
2. **Deleting consent does not revoke existing tokens**: Better Auth's `/oauth2/delete-consent` (`deleteConsentEndpoint`) deletes the `oauthConsent` row without deleting `oauthAccessToken` or `oauthRefreshToken` rows, and `revokeRefreshToken` marks `revoked = <timestamp>` rather than deleting the row. Moreover, `prepareBackchannelLogoutPlan` intentionally spares `offline_access` refresh tokens when a browser session is deleted, and `oauthAccessToken.sessionId` uses `ON DELETE SET NULL`. Therefore, `/mcp` must verify **both** the token row and an active `oauthConsent` grant row in D1.
3. **`banned` is not enforced on OAuth endpoints or token verification**: Consistent with ADR 0024, Better Auth's `admin` plugin only enforces `banned` in its `session.create.before` hook. Neither `validateJwtAccessToken`, `validateOpaqueAccessToken`, `/oauth2/authorize`, nor `handleRefreshTokenGrant` in `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` checks `user.banned`. Every `/mcp` request—and OAuth authorization/refresh hooks—must check `auth_user.banned` and `auth_user.banExpires` explicitly.
50→4. **`basePath: "/auth"` discovery & SPA asset routing**: `MainWorker.ts` sets `basePath: "/auth"` and forwards only `path.startsWith("/auth/") && !SURVEYBEAT_AUTH_PATHS.has(path)` to `authInstance.fetch`, while `WorkerWiring.ts` (`mainWorkerAssets.runWorkerFirst`) lists `/auth/*` and `/api/*`. However, `mcp()` serves RFC 9728 metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`, and `oauthProvider()` serves RFC 8414 metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/auth` (and `/auth/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`). Both `/.well-known/*` and `/mcp` must be added to `runWorkerFirst` and routed in `MainWorker.ts` before the SPA fallback.

                    └─ actorOf(directoryState, person.id) ─▶ Actor { personId, organizationAdmin, roles }
```

### Step-by-Step Resolution

1. **Consent-time Organization binding (`postLogin.consentReferenceId`)**:
   - During `/auth/oauth2/authorize`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider` runs `postLogin` after browser sign-in and before consent.
   - Using `D1PeopleIndex.linkedPersons(authUserId)` (and **not** Better Auth's `auth_organization` / `auth_member` tables, per ADR 0024), resolve the human's linked Organizations:
     - **Zero linked active Persons**: deny authorization (the human has no Organization membership to grant).
100→     - **One linked Organization**: `postLogin` passes automatically and `consentReferenceId` returns that `OrganizationId`.
     - **Multiple linked Organizations**: `postLogin` redirects to a SurveyBeat Organization-selection page (reusing the candidate-picker semantics from `SignInFlow.ts`), records the selected `OrganizationId` for the authorize continuation, and `consentReferenceId` returns it.
   - Better Auth persists that `OrganizationId` in `referenceId` on `auth_oauth_consent`, `auth_oauth_refresh_token`, and `auth_oauth_access_token`. Pinning each OAuth grant to one `OrganizationId` prevents an MCP client token from crossing Organizations or shifting silently when the human switches Organizations in the web app (`auth_session_organization`).
2. **Per-request D1 verification on `MainWorker` (auth plane)**:
   - Extract `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (reject missing/malformed tokens with `401` and RFC 9728 `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="..."`).
   - Compute the stored token digest matching Better Auth's `storeTokens` hash and execute a single D1 lookup joining `auth_oauth_access_token`, `auth_oauth_client`, `auth_oauth_consent`, `auth_user`, and (left join) `auth_session`:
     - Token row exists, `revoked IS NULL`, and `expiresAt > now`.
     - `auth_oauth_client` exists and `disabled = 0`.
     - **`auth_oauth_consent` row exists** matching `(clientId, userId, referenceId)` and covers the token's scopes. Consent coverage is not the audience check.
     - The token row's stored `resources` include the canonical MCP resource identifier. Better Auth 1.7.25 allows authorization with no resource (`packages/oauth-provider/src/oauth.ts` at that tag), so a token can have a valid consent and still not have been issued for `/mcp`.
110→     - If the token row's `confirmation` has a DPoP `jkt`, reject the request. `createOpaqueAccessToken` in `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` stores that key, and `confirmationTokenType` presents it as `DPoP`, not `Bearer`. This slice does not validate DPoP proofs or their replay cache. Do not advertise `dpop_bound_access_tokens` for the `/mcp` resource, and do not accept a sender-constrained token on the Bearer path.
     - If `sessionId IS NOT NULL` (or if `offline_access` was not granted), the `auth_session` row still exists and `expiresAt > now`.
     - **`auth_user.banned` check (ADR 0024)**: reject immediately if `banned = 1` and (`banExpires IS NULL` or `banExpires > now`). Also enforce the same `banned` check in `oauthProvider` hooks before `/oauth2/authorize`, `/oauth2/consent`, and `/oauth2/token` (`refresh_token` grant) so banned accounts cannot obtain or refresh tokens.
     - Verify `referenceId` is a non-empty `OrganizationId` (and check optional `person_index` existence).
3. **Per-request Organization DO verification (tenant & `Actor` plane)**:
   - Call the `Organization` Durable Object identified by `organizationId` (`referenceId`) to resolve the active `Person` and `Actor` (`organizationDirectory.activePerson(authUserId)` / `actorOf(directoryState, personId)` in `packages/domain/src/people/Directory.ts`).
   - The DO checks `person.auth_user_id = authUserId AND person.removed_at IS NULL` and computes `Actor { personId, organizationAdmin, roles }` from active `membership` rows (`ended_at IS NULL`).
   - If the `Person` was removed (`removed_at IS NOT NULL`) or deactivated, `activePerson` / `actorOf` returns `None`, and `/mcp` immediately fails the request (`401` / `403`).
   - Every MCP tool passes `Actor` (or `actorId` + DO enforcement) through the existing domain permission function `can(actor, action, resource)` and privacy rules (minimum group size, subtraction-safe roll-ups, comment redaction, Lead-only discussion guides, review windows).
   - The same call also requires the token's stored scopes to include the scope mapped to that tool. `can` in `packages/domain/src/people/Permissions.ts` does not see OAuth scopes. A read-only token must fail a write even when the `Person` is an Organization admin.
120→
### Revocation Semantics (ADR 0023)

- **No deny list**: Consistent with ADR 0023 (which deleted `revoked_session`), revocation deletes the grant/token rows directly in D1; no deny-list table is added.
- **Immediate failure on next request**:
  - **User revokes an MCP client grant**: delete the `auth_oauth_consent` row **and** the matching `auth_oauth_access_token` and `auth_oauth_refresh_token` rows for `(clientId, userId, referenceId)` in one `database.batch([...])` call. The stock `deleteConsentEndpoint` in `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` (`oauthConsent/endpoints.ts`) deletes only the consent row. Do not mount that endpoint unchanged. ### Step-by-Step Resolution
```

1. **Consent-time Organization binding (`postLogin.consentReferenceId`)**:
   - During `/auth/oauth2/authorize`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider` runs `postLogin` after browser sign-in and before consent.
   - Using `D1PeopleIndex.linkedPersons(authUserId)` (and **not** Better Auth's `auth_organization` / `auth_member` tables, per ADR 0024), resolve the human's linked Organizations:
     - **Zero linked active Persons**: deny authorization (the human has no Organization membership to grant).
     - **One linked Organization**: `postLogin` passes automatically and `consentReferenceId` returns that `OrganizationId`.
     - **Multiple linked Organizations**: `postLogin` redirects to a SurveyBeat Organization-selection page (reusing the candidate-picker semantics from `SignInFlow.ts`), records the selected `OrganizationId` for the authorize continuation, and `consentReferenceId` returns it.
   - Better Auth persists that `OrganizationId` in `referenceId` on `auth_oauth_consent`, `auth_oauth_refresh_token`, and `auth_oauth_access_token`. Pinning each OAuth grant to one `OrganizationId` prevents an MCP client token from crossing Organizations or shifting silently when the human switches Organizations in the web app (`auth_session_organization`).
2. **Per-request D1 verification on `MainWorker` (auth plane)**:
   - Extract `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (reject missing/malformed tokens with `401` and RFC 9728 `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="..."`).
   - Compute the stored token digest matching Better Auth's `storeTokens` hash and execute a single D1 lookup joining `auth_oauth_access_token`, `auth_oauth_client`, `auth_oauth_consent`, `auth_user`, and (left join) `auth_session`:
     - Token row exists, `revoked IS NULL`, and `expiresAt > now`.
     - `auth_oauth_client` exists and `disabled = 0`.
     - **`auth_oauth_consent` row exists** matching `(clientId, userId, referenceId)` and covers the token's scopes. Consent coverage is not the audience check.
     - The token row's stored `resources` include the canonical MCP resource identifier. Better Auth 1.7.25 allows authorization with no resource (`packages/oauth-provider/src/oauth.ts` at that tag), so a token can have a valid consent and still not have been issued for `/mcp`.
     - If the token row's `confirmation` has a DPoP `jkt`, reject the request. `createOpaqueAccessToken` in `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` stores that key, and `confirmationTokenType` presents it as `DPoP`, not `Bearer`. This slice does not validate DPoP proofs or their replay cache. Do not advertise `dpop_bound_access_tokens` for the `/mcp` resource, and do not accept a sender-constrained token on the Bearer path.
     - If `sessionId IS NOT NULL` (or if `offline_access` was not granted), the `auth_session` row still exists and `expiresAt > now`.
     - **`auth_user.banned` check (ADR 0024)**: reject immediately if `banned = 1` and (`banExpires IS NULL` or `banExpires > now`). Also enforce the same `banned` check in `oauthProvider` hooks before `/oauth2/authorize`, `/oauth2/consent`, and `/oauth2/token` (`refresh_token` grant) so banned accounts cannot obtain or refresh tokens.
     - Verify `referenceId` is a non-empty `OrganizationId` (and check optional `person_index` existence).
3. **Per-request Organization DO verification (tenant & `Actor` plane)**:
   - Call the `Organization` Durable Object identified by `organizationId` (`referenceId`) to resolve the active `Person` and `Actor` (`organizationDirectory.activePerson(authUserId)` / `actorOf(directoryState, personId)` in `packages/domain/src/people/Directory.ts`).
   - The DO checks `person.auth_user_id = authUserId AND person.removed_at IS NULL` and computes `Actor { personId, organizationAdmin, roles }` from active `membership` rows (`ended_at IS NULL`).
   - If the `Person` was removed (`removed_at IS NOT NULL`) or deactivated, `activePerson` / `actorOf` returns `None`, and `/mcp` immediately fails the request (`401` / `403`).
   - Every MCP tool passes `Actor` (or `actorId` + DO enforcement) through the existing domain permission function `can(actor, action, resource)` and privacy rules (minimum group size, subtraction-safe roll-ups, comment redaction, Lead-only discussion guides, review windows).
   - The same call also requires the token's stored scopes to include the scope mapped to that tool. `can` in `packages/domain/src/people/Permissions.ts` does not see OAuth scopes. A read-only token must fail a write even when the `Person` is an Organization admin.

### Revocation Semantics (ADR 0023)

- **No deny list**: Consistent with ADR 0023 (which deleted `revoked_session`), revocation deletes the grant/token rows directly in D1; no deny-list table is added.
- **Immediate failure on next request**:
  - **User revokes an MCP client grant**: delete the `auth_oauth_consent` row **and** the matching `auth_oauth_access_token` and `auth_oauth_refresh_token` rows for `(clientId, userId, referenceId)` in one `database.batch([...])` call. The stock `deleteConsentEndpoint` in `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` (`oauthConsent/endpoints.ts`) deletes only the consent row. Do not mount that endpoint unchanged. A later grant for the same client and Organization inserts a new consent row, and an unexpired old token would pass the consent join. Because the `/mcp` verifier requires both the access-token row and the consent row, deleting both makes the next request fail with `401 invalid_token`.
  - **OAuth client calls `/oauth2/revoke`**: `revokeOpaqueAccessToken` deletes the `auth_oauth_access_token` row immediately; `revokeRefreshToken` marks `revoked` on `auth_oauth_refresh_token` and deletes linked `auth_oauth_access_token` rows.
  - **Admin bans a user (`banUser`) or removes a Person (`RemovePerson`)**: `auth_user.banned = 1` and `person.removed_at != NULL` both fail the very next `/mcp` request immediately, and the workflow should also delete matching `auth_oauth_consent`, `auth_oauth_access_token`, and `auth_oauth_refresh_token` rows in D1 (`userId` / `(userId, referenceId)`) so no stale refresh grant lingers.

### D1 (`packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations/0011_better_auth_mcp.sql` + `d1-migrations.lock.json`)

D1 remains strictly the global auth/routing index—**no survey content** (no Pulses, Rounds, Submissions, Answers, Results, Themes, Actions, or Notes) is ever stored in D1.

| `auth_oauth_client` | Registered MCP clients (CIMD/DCR/static) | `clientId` (unique), `redirectUris`, `scopes`, `tokenEndpointAuthMethod`, `requirePKCE`, `disabled`, `userId` |

1→# Remote MCP Authentication and Streamable HTTP Transport on MainWorker

Research for [issue #301](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/301). Checked on 2026-11-20 against repo pins `better-auth@1.7.25`, `effect@4.1.4`, and `@alchemy.run/cloudflare@2.0.0-beta.87`, plus published npm tarballs for `@better-auth/mcp@1.7.25`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25`, `@better-auth/core@1.7.25`, `@better-auth/cimd@1.7.25`, `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@1.2.4`, and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.32.2`.

> [!NOTE]
> `node_modules` was not materialized on initial checkout, so Better Auth 1.7.25 and candidate package internals were verified directly from the published npm package tarballs for the exact repo pins and cross-checked against `packages/auth`, `packages/cloudflare`, `packages/domain`, and `docs/adr/`. `SPEC.md` and `docs/adr/` were not modified (issue #296 owns the `SPEC.md` release-order update).

## 1. Recommendation

10→1. **OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + Consent (`@better-auth/mcp@1.7.25`)**: Add **`@better-auth/mcp@1.7.25`** (which wraps **`@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25`**, plus **`@better-auth/cimd@1.7.25`** if Client ID Metadata Documents are enabled) to SurveyBeat's existing Better Auth configuration in `packages/auth` on D1.
   - Configure `mcp({ disableJwtPlugin: true, ... })` so access tokens are **opaque** (stored by hash in D1) rather than stateless JWTs, and validate `/mcp` Bearer tokens on `MainWorker` directly against D1 rather than relying solely on `@better-auth/mcp`'s `requireMcpAuth`.
   - Reject `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@1.2.4`: it requires a dedicated Cloudflare KV namespace (`OAUTH_KV`), duplicating auth state outside D1 (violating SPEC §6.2's "Do not use [KV] for sessions that must be revoked at once" and ADR 0022's single-provider rule).
2. **MCP Server & Streamable HTTP Transport (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.32.2`)**: Serve `POST /mcp` on `MainWorker` using `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js` (`Server`) and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.js` (`WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport`) in **stateless per-request mode** (`sessionIdGenerator: undefined`, `enableJsonResponse: true`), initialized with `CfWorkerJsonSchemaValidator` (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/validation/cfworker`) and wrapped by a thin Effect adapter that generates tool JSON Schemas and validates tool inputs/outputs with **Effect Schema**.
   - Do **not** adopt `effect/ai/McpServer` (`effect@4.1.4`) yet: its stateless `McpServer.layerHttpRequestScoped` rejects every protocol older than `2026-07-28`, while its `2025-11-25`/`2025-03-26` `McpServer.layerHttp` stores `mcp-session-id` in an isolate-local `Map` and forks a background fiber.

---

## 2. Better Auth 1.7.25 Package Name & OAuth Comparison

20→### Confirmed Package Name at Pin `1.7.25`

Inspecting `better-auth@1.7.25` (`dist/plugins/index.d.mts`) confirms that **`better-auth/plugins` does not export an `mcp` plugin**. At `1.7.25`, Better Auth ships MCP support as separate scoped packages pinned alongside `better-auth`:

| Package (`1.7.25`) | Role at `1.7.25` | Key dependencies / exports |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `better-auth` (`1.7.25`) | Core auth, `emailOTP`, `magicLink`, `admin`, `organization`, `jwt` | No `mcp` export in `better-auth/plugins` |
| `@better-auth/mcp` (`1.7.25`) | **Real MCP plugin package**; wraps `oauthProvider` for RFC 9728 / RFC 8707 | Depends on `@better-auth/oauth-provider@^1.7.25`, `jose@^6.1.3`; exports `mcp`, `requireMcpAuth`, `createMcpProtectedRequestHandler` |
| `@better-auth/oauth-provider` (`1.7.25`) | Underlying OAuth 2.1 / OIDC Authorization Server plugin | Peer-depends on `better-auth@^1.7.25`, `@better-auth/core@^1.7.25`; exports `oauthProvider`, metadata helpers |
| `@better-auth/cimd` (`1.7.25`) | Client ID Metadata Documents (`draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document-00`) | Optional companion for MCP 2026-07-28 client registration |

I will revise the KV cell line 39 to avoid leading with "Immediate".

The KV cell will clarify that revocation is not immediate across locations. Line 115 will add the `activePerson` path, calling the `Organization` Durable Object to resolve the active `Person` and `Actor`.

The `activePerson` method is implemented in `packages/cloudflare/src/organization/Directory.ts`. The `actorOf` helper lives in `packages/domain/src/people/Directory.ts`.

With `disableJwtPlugin: true`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` requires six `auth_`-prefixed tables. Map them in `AUTH_TABLES` in `packages/auth/src/options.ts`. No `jwks` table is needed.

I am now identifying the best places to add the sign-out gap.

SurveyBeat's sign-out deletes the session row with raw SQL. This skips Better Auth's `session.delete` hooks. `prepareBackchannelLogoutPlan` never runs. Refresh tokens are not revoked on sign-out. The session check must treat a missing session as failure.

The existing session check catches the sign-out gap. A token without `offline_access` must have a live session, but its `sessionId` is now NULL. The `/mcp` verifier and refresh path rely on this check, so implementation slice #302 should be told.

Slice #302 may also record the `/mcp`-only ban check in an ADR, since it extends beyond ADR 0024's web-path rule.

SQLite and D1 still fire the `ON DELETE SET NULL` foreign key trigger on the session row even when the deletion is raw SQL.

The existing session check already guards against the sign-out gap. It requires the `auth_session` row to still exist when `sessionId` is not NULL or `offline_access` was not granted. This prevents a missing session from passing when `offline_access` was absent.

I will add a revocation bullet and tighten the session-check bullet. The refresh path must rely on the live-session check too, since refresh tokens survive sign-out because Better Auth hooks do not run. I will also add a short note about the ADR for the banned-path check.

The revocation bullet will cite `SessionIdentityProvider.deleteSession` in `packages/cloudflare/src/MainWorker.ts` as the raw SQL sign-out path.

ADR 0024 limits Better Auth's `banned` enforcement to web endpoints. Checking `auth_user.banned` on every `/mcp` request is a new surface. Issue #302 should record that rule if it adopts it. I will phrase this as a note for #302 rather than a decision requiring an ADR. The standing instruction is to avoid pre-deciding later grilling.

- **Admin bans a user (`banUser`) or removes a Person (`RemovePerson`)**: `auth_user.banned = 1` and `person.removed_at != NULL` both fail the very next `/mcp` request immediately, and the workflow should also delete matching `auth_oauth_consent`, `auth_oauth_access_token`, and `auth_oauth_refresh_token` rows in D1 (`userId` / `(userId, referenceId)`) so no stale refresh grant lingers.
  - **Browser sign-out does not revoke MCP tokens**: `SessionIdentityProvider.deleteSession` in `packages/cloudflare/src/MainWorker.ts` runs `DELETE FROM auth_session WHERE id = ?`. That skips Better Auth's `session.delete` hooks, so `prepareBackchannelLogoutPlan` never runs and no refresh token is revoked, `offline_access` or not. The access-token foreign key then sets `sessionId` to NULL. Issue #302's `/mcp` verifier and refresh path have to rely on the live-session check above: a token without `offline_access` fails once its session row is gone.

- **Immediate failure on next request**:
  - **User revokes an MCP client grant**: delete the `auth_oauth_consent` row **and** the matching `auth_oauth_access_token` and `auth_oauth_refresh_token` rows for `(clientId, userId, referenceId)` in one `database.batch([...])` call. The stock `deleteConsentEndpoint` in `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` (`oauthConsent/endpoints.ts`) deletes only the consent row. Do not mount that endpoint unchanged. A later grant for the same client and Organization inserts a new consent row, and an unexpired old token would pass the consent join. Because the `/mcp` verifier requires both the access-token row and the consent row, deleting both makes the next request fail with `401 invalid_token`.

Ports 1337 and 1338 are currently held by other agents' vitest runs.

I will not start the commit gate now. I will set up a silent monitor to wake when ports 1337 and 1338 are free and no gate or vitest process is running. I must commit before another agent grabs those ports.

The monitor will poll every 30 seconds. It will only print when no gate or vitest unit process is running and ports 1337 and 1338 are free. A race between wake and commit is acceptable; a failed commit will trigger a retry. Several gates have been running for 7–12 minutes, and the unit suite is long. Organization.test.ts binds port 1338 near the end.

Ports being free does not mean a suite has finished. The previous failure happened because a suite reached Organization.test while the monitor was idle. The safe condition is zero `vitest run --project unit` and zero `gate.mjs` processes anywhere. I will write a 30-second polling monitor script.

The monitor will log its status to a file. I will also draft the CodeRabbit comment text while waiting, but I will not post it until the commit lands.

I will check the GDPR 313 worktree status next. I will not poll the 305 or 297 delegates. I may check GitHub for new PRs from those workers as bookkeeping.

I will check open PRs for 305 or 297 while waiting. I will not update the memory topic surveybeat-mcp-auth.md until after the commit succeeds. The monitor script will be placed in ~/.grok/long-running-background-tasks/.

I verified the six-plus-one optional table count. I will not start the 313 commit yet. The monitor will exit immediately upon waking so the turn ends cleanly.

The monitor script will log its status to a file so a log line is never mistaken for DONE. I will check the GDPR 313 worktree and open PRs in parallel while waiting. I will also fetch the CodeRabbit comment bodies for replies. The three comment IDs are 4639722692, 4639722699, and 4639722708.

I will fetch the full CodeRabbit comment bodies via `gh api` so my replies address the actual feedback. I will not reply to the comments until the commit lands, because the commit SHA is needed to reference the fix. I will save the comment text to context so the next turn can post the replies immediately upon waking.

  busy=$(ps -eo cmd | grep -E "scripts/fence/gate.mjs|vitest run --project unit" | grep -v grep | wc -l)

done
EOF

echo "script ready"

Opus approved PR 317. The research note now matches that review, and the commit is waiting until the local worker ports are free.

The note in `docs/research/r3-mcp-auth.md` now says:

- `activePerson` is `OrganizationPeople.activePerson` in `packages/domain/src/people/SignInPorts.ts`, implemented on the Organization Durable Object in `packages/cloudflare/src/organization/Directory.ts`. Only `actorOf` lives in the domain `Directory.ts`.
- OAuth storage is six `auth_` tables, plus optional `auth_oauth_client_assertion`.
- KV revocation is not immediate across locations.
- Sign-out runs `DELETE FROM auth_session WHERE id = ?` in `MainWorker.ts`, so Better Auth session-delete hooks never run. Issue #302 has to keep the live-session check on `/mcp` and on refresh, including for tokens without `offline_access`. The `/mcp` ban check may need its own ADR beyond ADR 0024.

The CodeRabbit constraints (audience, DPoP rejection, per-tool scopes, and deleting tokens with the consent row) stay in the note. No second Opus review for these edits.

PR 316's Deploy succeeded for `5366d18f`. The GDPR 313 docs are still staged and uncommitted. Other agents are running unit suites on ports 1337 and 1338, so this commit waits for those to finish, then pushes and replies on the four CodeRabbit threads.

**Note:** `docs/research/r3-vercel-chat-adapters.md`
**Checks and reviews:** not yet reported; CI had just started.

**Recommendation:** use thin custom Effect adapters for Slack and Teams behind the domain `ChannelSender` port. Don't adopt the `vercel/chat` runtime or its `StateAdapter`. The full adapters do load in workerd, but the Teams adapter alone is about 897 KiB gzip and took 1.8 s of startup CPU in the one local profile that finished, against the 1 s limit. The official state stores (Redis, Postgres) would break SPEC §6. A Durable Object SQLite state adapter exists only in Cloudflare's separate `agents` package, and the thin route doesn't need one.

Other findings:
- **Slack:** a button with a `url` still sends `block_actions`; plain links are not interactive components. Slack never says in words that plain links send nothing, so that conclusion rests on its payload list.
- **Teams conversation reference:** it belongs in the Organization Durable Object. D1 holds only the tenant-to-Organization routing row.
- **Inbound JWT check:** the Teams adapter's stateless subpath doesn't verify the inbound token, so we would write that check either way.

**Not verified:**
- **Teams Safe Links and the `#t=…&v=…` fragment.** I had no Defender-licensed tenant. The note cites Microsoft's docs (links are checked at click time, not rewritten, nothing about fragments) and gives a test plan. If the fragment is lost, both `#t=` and `&v=` go with it, so Teams has no way to hand the Invitation to the answer page; the note treats that as blocking.
- **Teams cross-tenant sending.** Microsoft deprecated new multi-tenant bots in July 2025, and I found no Microsoft document saying whether a single-tenant bot can send into other customers' tenants. The only evidence is two Microsoft Q&A threads. The note says Teams needs a tenancy spike before the ADR commits to it.
- **Real traffic.** I had no Slack workspace or Azure Bot, so I checked bundling, loading and the 401 rejection paths in local workerd. I did not check a valid inbound event or an outbound send.
- **Alchemy.** Nothing was deployed through it.
- **Startup times.** They come from a shared, noisy machine and varied up to 4× between runs.

**Version control deviations:**
- **`but` missing.** It is not on PATH here, though it worked on the first call. I committed on the checked-out branch with plain `git` and the pre-commit hook ran with no `--no-verify`. I pushed with an explicit refspec and opened the PR with `gh pr create --base main` instead of `but pr new`. I linked the PR in T3.
- **Stray `pkill`.** One of my early `pkill -f workerd` calls could have killed other local workerd processes, for example another agent's `alchemy dev`.

1: # Can vercel/chat run SurveyBeat's Slack and Microsoft Teams Channels?
2: 
3: Research for issue #297 (map #295, Release 3). Researched 2026-11-20 against `chat`, `@chat-adapter/slack` and `@chat-adapter/teams` **4.45.0** (published 2026-11-13). This note changes no code, adds no dependency and edits neither `SPEC.md` nor any ADR. The Channel ADR (numbers 0027+) takes its constraints from §4.
4: 
5: Claims marked *(secondary)* come from a forum or Q&A thread, not from vendor documentation. Claims marked *(measured)* come from the throwaway probes described in §2.1, which are not committed.
6: 
7: ## 1. Recommendation
8: 
9: **Use thin custom Effect adapters for Slack and Microsoft Teams behind the domain `ChannelSender` port. Do not adopt the `Chat` runtime, its `StateAdapter`, or the full `@chat-adapter/*` packages.**
10: 
11: The `Chat` runtime is built for conversational bots (threads, subscriptions, locks, message dedupe), and R3's Channel work is outbound-first plus one slash command. The full adapters do run in workerd (*measured*), but the Teams adapter alone adds about 897 KiB gzip and spent 1.8 s of active startup CPU in the one local profile that finished, against a 1 s Worker startup limit; the `Chat` runtime also needs a `StateAdapter` that SurveyBeat has no Cloudflare-native, tenant-isolated implementation of.
12: 
13: What to build, in order:
14: 
15: 1. **Slack first**, as #295 sequences it. About five endpoints are needed: signature verification (Web Crypto HMAC), `oauth.v2.access`, `chat.postMessage`, `chat.update`/`chat.delete`, and `users.lookupByEmail`. All are plain `fetch` calls validated with Effect Schema at the boundary.
16: 2. **Teams second, behind a tenancy spike** (§3.6). The Azure Bot tenancy rules changed in 2025 and a single-tenant bot may not reach other customers' tenants. This is the largest unresolved risk in R3.
17: 3. **No external store, no `StateAdapter`.** Everything an outbound-first Channel needs (installation token, Person-to-Channel binding, sent-message id for later edits) is Organization state and belongs in the Organization Durable Object beside the existing `SendStore`. Redis would break SPEC §6; the Durable Object SQLite `StateAdapter` that exists today ships in Cloudflare's `agents` package, not in `vercel/chat` (§3.3), and is not worth taking on for a surface this narrow.
18: 4. **Treat `@chat-adapter/{slack,teams}` as reference and test vectors**, not as a dependency. Their stateless subpath modules (`/webhook`, `/api`, `/blocks`, `/cards`) are small, MIT, `fetch`-based and run in workerd with 13.1 KiB gzip (*measured*). Our code is smaller than the cost of tracking a package that shipped seven minor releases between 2026-08-14 and 2026-11-13. If the Channel ADR prefers to reuse them, it must name the package, as AGENTS.md requires, and pin an exact version.
19: 
20: **Revisit this if** a later release wants in-chat conversation (threads, "reply to answer", streaming). Then `chat` plus Cloudflare's `agents/chat-sdk` state adapter is the route to evaluate, and #295's exclusion of in-chat Answer submission would need its own ADR.
21: 
22: ## 2. Answers to the issue's questions
23: 
24: | Question | Answer | Basis |
25: | --- | --- | --- |
26: | Does `vercel/chat` run on Workers with Alchemy and Effect 4.1.x (`nodejs_compat`)? | Yes, mechanically. `wrangler deploy --dry-run` bundles Slack, Teams and both together, and local workerd serves and rejects bad signatures. It is promise-based, so every call is wrapped in `Effect.tryPromise`. No Alchemy-specific obstacle was found, but I did not deploy through Alchemy. | §2.1, *measured* |
27: | Workerd compatibility and footprint? | Slack full: 277 KiB gz. Teams full: 897 KiB gz, 1.8 s active startup in the one local profile that finished (two others timed out at 10 s). Both: 996 KiB gz. Stateless subpaths: 13 KiB gz. Worker size limit is 64 MiB, so **startup time, not size, is the limiter.** | §2.1, *measured* |
28: | Signature verification and stateless handling in `MainWorker`? | Slack: HMAC-SHA256 with Web Crypto, 5-minute skew, no state. Teams: Microsoft's JWT check, which the stateless subpath does **not** implement; we write it. | §3.2 |
29: | Does it need Redis or another external store? | The `Chat` constructor requires a `StateAdapter`; official ones are Redis, ioredis, Postgres, memory. Redis and Postgres are third-party stores and break SPEC §6. A DO SQLite `StateAdapter` exists but is Cloudflare's `agents/chat-sdk`, not part of `vercel/chat`. With thin adapters, **no `StateAdapter` is required.** | §3.3 |
30: | Card fidelity? | Slack Block Kit and Teams Adaptive Cards both carry what R3 needs: rating links, a Reminder, a Result summary, and later edits. Plain-link Invitations are possible on both. | §3.4 |
31: | Slack app and Teams bot registration and per-Organization OAuth install? | Slack: standard distributed app plus OAuth v2 install per workspace. Teams: Entra app plus Azure Bot plus Teams app package; per-tenant admin install; tenancy model unresolved. | §3.5, §3.6 |
32: | Teams proactive messages, and where does the conversation reference live? | Needs the bot installed in the Person's personal scope, plus tenant id, user id and service URL. Store the per-Person reference in the **Organization Durable Object**; D1 holds only the tenant-to-Organization routing row. | §3.6 |
33: | Safe Links and the fragment `#t=…&v=…`? | **Not tested.** Microsoft documents that Teams links are checked at click time and not rewritten, and says nothing about fragments. Treat as unverified and gating for Teams. | §3.7 |
34: | Slack plain links and `block_actions`? | Slack documents `block_actions` as the payload for Block Kit interactive components, and a URL button still sends one. Plain `<url\|text>` links in message text are not interactive components. **Slack does not state "plain links send nothing" in so many words;** the conclusion follows from its payload list and is a one-click live check. | §3.8 |
35: 
36: ### 2.1 How the footprint was measured
37: 
38: In a scratch directory outside the repository I installed the four 4.45.0 packages (plus `@chat-adapter/state-memory`) and wrote five tiny Worker entries. Each used `compatibility_date = 2026-11-01` and `nodejs_compat`, wrangler 4.165.0, Node 26.
39: 
40: | Entry | `wrangler deploy --dry-run` | Local `wrangler check startup`, active CPU |
41: | --- | --- | --- |
42: | Stateless subpaths only (`slack/webhook`, `slack/api`, `slack/blocks`, `teams/api`, `teams/cards`, `teams/webhook`) | 56.5 KiB / **13.1 KiB gz** | 19 / 99 / 59 ms |
43: | `Chat` + Slack adapter + memory state | 1,324 KiB / **277 KiB gz** | 232 / 93 / 63 ms |
44: | `Chat` + Teams adapter + memory state | 4,839 KiB / **897 KiB gz** | 1,795 ms; the other two runs timed out at 10 s |
45: | `Chat` + Slack + Teams + memory state | 5,332 KiB / **996 KiB gz** | 952 / 449 / 700 ms |
46: | For scale: Effect HttpApi Worker (`docs/research/effect-on-workers.md`) | about 86 KiB gz | 54–61 ms |
47: 
48: Caveats that matter:
49: 
50: - Startup numbers are **local workerd on a shared, noisy machine**, so they are indicative only. Cloudflare warns that production CPUs differ, and `docs/research/effect-on-workers.md` makes the same point. The Worker startup limit is 1 s ([Workers limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/)). A Teams adapter that sometimes needs more than a second locally is not a safe thing to load into `MainWorker`.
51: - The Worker size limit on both plans is 64 MiB (same page), so 1 MiB gzip is not a size problem. It is a startup-parse and review-surface problem.
52: - Behaviour check in local workerd: `bot.webhooks.slack` returned `401 Invalid signature` for a bad signature, and `bot.webhooks.teams` returned `401` for a missing `Authorization` header. That proves the modules load and the rejection path works. **It does not prove a valid inbound activity or an outbound send**, which need real Slack and Azure credentials.
53: - Why the Teams adapter is so heavy: its dependencies are `@microsoft/teams.apps` (needs Node ≥ 22.12; depends on `express`, `axios`, `jsonwebtoken`, `jwks-rsa`, `@azure/msal-node`, `@microsoft/signalr`, `reflect-metadata`) plus `teams.api`, `teams.cards`, `teams.graph` and `teams.graph-endpoints` ([npm metadata](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/teams.apps)). Slack's full adapter pulls `@slack/web-api` and `@slack/socket-mode`.
54: 
55: ## 3. Evidence
56: 
57: ### 3.1 What `vercel/chat` is
58: 
59: - Chat SDK is a TypeScript bot framework: a `Chat` instance holds platform adapters and one state adapter; handlers such as `bot.onNewMention` and `onSubscribedMessage` run for events from every adapter, and each adapter exposes `bot.webhooks.<name>` ([Vercel docs](https://vercel.com/docs/chat-sdk/adapters)). Repository: [vercel/chat](https://github.com/vercel/chat), MIT.
60: - The state adapter "share[s] subscriptions, locks, and cached data across requests" (same page). Core `Chat` calls it on every inbound message: `setIfNotExists` for `dedupe:<adapter>:<messageId>` and `acquireLock` per thread (read in `chat@4.45.0` `dist/index.js`).
61: - Release cadence is fast: 4.38.0 on 2026-08-14 to 4.45.0 on 2026-11-13. The docs warn that protected members of official adapters "can change in minor releases, so pin the adapter version" ([Vercel docs](https://vercel.com/docs/chat-sdk/adapters)).
62: - The repo already pins Effect and Alchemy together because both are unstable or beta (ADR 0008). A third fast-moving dependency in the send path is a cost, not a saving, for a surface of about five calls per platform.
63: 
64: ### 3.2 Webhook verification and stateless handling in `MainWorker`
65: 
66: **Slack.** Requests carry `x-slack-request-timestamp` and `x-slack-signature`; the adapter verifies `v0=` + HMAC-SHA256 over `v0:<timestamp>:<body>` with `crypto.subtle`, and rejects a timestamp more than 300 s off (`@chat-adapter/slack@4.45.0`, `dist/chunk-KYABMAGK.js`). This is stateless and about 40 lines in Effect with Web Crypto. Slack must receive an acknowledgement within 3 seconds for interaction payloads ([handling user interaction](https://docs.slack.dev/interactivity/handling-user-interaction/)); a slash command should ack immediately and post the answer through `response_url`, which accepts up to 5 posts within 30 minutes (same page). `MainWorker` must read the raw body once and verify before parsing.
67: 
68: **Teams.** Microsoft requires the bot to verify a JWT on every inbound request: `Authorization: Bearer`, issuer `https://api.botframework.com`, audience equal to the bot's app id, within validity (5-minute skew), RS256 signature from the keys at `https://login.botframework.com/v1/.well-known/keys`, and a `serviceUrl` claim equal to the activity's `serviceUrl`. The page calls requirements 4 and 6 (signature and serviceUrl) "particularly" important ([Bot Connector authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/rest-api/bot-framework-rest-connector-authentication)). The stateless `@chat-adapter/teams/webhook` subpath **only parses** activities; it contains no JWT, JWKS or OpenID code (grep of the 4.45.0 `dist`). JWT verification lives in the heavy `@microsoft/teams.apps` path. So the thin route has to write this check either way. It needs `crypto.subtle` RS256 verify, a cached JWKS fetch, and the `serviceUrl` claim match. The single-tenant variant (tenant-specific issuer and metadata) was not confirmed from documentation; see §5.
69: 
70: **Useful guard to copy from the Teams adapter:** it refuses to send a bot token to any `serviceUrl` outside an allowlist (`smba.trafficmanager.net` and the GCC, DoD and China hosts) or a loopback emulator (`dist/chunk-4NNW2LU4.js`). `serviceUrl` arrives in the inbound activity, so an unchecked value is a token-exfiltration path.
71: 
72: **Where it runs.** Both verifications are request-local and stateless, so they can sit in `MainWorker` beside the Better Auth routes, with each route's classification added to `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts`. The Submission Worker stays untouched; no Channel traffic may reach it (ADR 0005).
73: 
74: ### 3.3 State storage
75: 
76: - `Chat` takes `state` in its config and uses it for dedupe and locks (§3.1). The official state adapters are Redis, ioredis, PostgreSQL and memory; the docs tell Vercel deployments to use Redis, ioredis or PostgreSQL, because memory "loses state on restart and two instances can process the same thread at once" ([Vercel docs](https://vercel.com/docs/chat-sdk/adapters)). **Redis and Postgres are third-party stores and break SPEC §6, so `vercel/chat` cannot be used with its official state adapters.**
77: - A Durable Object SQLite adapter does exist, but it is not part of `vercel/chat`. Cloudflare's `agents` package exports `createChatSdkState()` and a `ChatSdkStateAgent` sub-agent that store subscriptions, locks, queues, dedupe keys, thread state and history in Durable Object SQLite ([Cloudflare docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/agent-class/communication-channels/chat-sdk/); listed as vendor-official in [vercel/chat#669](https://github.com/vercel/chat/issues/669)). Costs for SurveyBeat:
78:   - it requires the `agents` package (version 0.33.0 today; peer dependencies include `ai`, `zod`, `chat`, `react` and `vite`), a parent `Agent` Durable Object class, and the `ChatSdkStateAgent` class exported from the Worker entry. SurveyBeat's classes come from Alchemy's generated entry (AGENTS.md notes the same constraint for #247), so this is untested friction;
79:   - state shards are keyed by platform thread or channel id (`slack:C123`), not by Organization, so chat state would live **outside** the per-Organization Durable Object that SPEC §6.2 makes the system of record;
80:   - `vercel/chat` itself does not consider the adapter part of its CLI scaffold (`CLI_INCOMPATIBLE_ADAPTERS` in #669), so it is a supported-but-unusual combination.
84: ### 3.4 Card fidelity
101: ### 3.5 Slack app and per-Organization install
111: ### 3.6 Teams registration, proactive messages, and the tenancy risk
134: ### 3.7 Teams Safe Links and the URL fragment
154: ### 3.8 Slack: plain links and `block_actions`

176: ## 5. What I could not verify

This note changes no code, adds no dependency and edits neither `SPEC.md` nor any ADR. The Channel ADR (numbers 0027+) takes its constraints from §4.
