details.context_before: Fidelity is not what separates the options: the Chat SDK's card model compiles to the same Block Kit and Adaptive Card JSON we would write by hand, and its `link` element is already the plain-link form. Two limits to check in the spike, neither verified here: the maximum number of actions per Adaptive Card in Teams (five rating `Action.OpenUrl` buttons plus "Open check-in" may hit it, in which case use markdown links in a `TextBlock`), and Teams link-preview behaviour for URLs in plain text messages (a preview fetch carries no fragment, so it is harmless to the token, but it would show a title).
details.context_after: ### 3.5 Slack app and per-Organization install
details.line_prefix: **Why plain links are a privacy requirement, not just a style choice.** A Slack button click sends `block_actions` to `MainWorker`, with the clicking Slack user id and a timestamp. That is a Person-bound, timed event for "opened the rating link on Round R" at the moment of answering, delivered to the Worker that has logs, while ADR 0005 keeps all of that off the Submission path.

**Tenancy: the open problem.**

- Microsoft's registration page says multi-tenant bot creation "will be deprecated after July 31, 2025": existing multi-tenant bots keep working but new ones cannot be created; use single-tenant or user-assigned managed identity ([Register a bot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/bot-service-quickstart-registration)). The adapter's own default is `appType: "MultiTenant"`, which is a deprecated mode for a newly created bot.
details.context_after:

**Proactive messages.**

content.text:
114→
**Tenancy: the open problem.**

- Microsoft's registration page says multi-tenant bot creation "will be deprecated after July 31, 2025": existing multi-tenant bots keep working but new ones cannot be created; use single-tenant or user-assigned managed identity ([Register a bot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/bot-service-quickstart-registration)). The adapter's own default is `appType: "MultiTenant"`, which is a deprecated mode for a newly created bot.
- SurveyBeat must send to Persons in **many customers' tenants** from one bot. A Microsoft Q&A thread *(secondary)* from an ISV with about 100 tenants says the documented single-tenant model "does not provide the cross-tenant outbound capability" their SaaS needs; ([Q&A 5896006](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5896006/request-for-exception-to-provision-new-multi-tenan)). The workaround lists on that page come from two moderators: a single-tenant bot distributed as a Teams app that other tenants install, a user-assigned managed identity, or a newer Microsoft 365 Agents route. The MVP answer offers no workaround and says only Microsoft can grant an exception. Who wrote the Microsoft 365 Agent / Copilot extensibility mention was not confirmed. None of those answers states that single-tenant outbound to other tenants works. Another thread *(secondary)* says publishing through AppSource is "strongly recommended" for external tenants with a single-tenant bot, and the same answer says that a proactive message into another tenant uses a token that is not valid there, so the Bot Framework rejects the request ([Q&A 5882874](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5882874/clarification-on-multi-tenant-support-for-single-t)). That rejection is still secondary, and it is the most direct statement found on the open question.
- **I found no Microsoft document that settles whether one single-tenant bot can mint a token and send proactive messages into customer tenants.** This must be resolved by a spike with two real tenants before the ADR commits to Teams; the fallbacks (a bot registration per customer tenant, or only Teams-installed-by-the-tenant scenarios) change the cost and the install story materially.
120→
**Proactive messages.**

- The bot must be installed for the user in the personal scope; otherwise the create-conversation call fails with 403 `ForbiddenOperationException` ([proactive messages](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/bots/how-to/conversations/send-proactive-messages)). The page offers two ways to install: proactively through Microsoft Graph, or a custom app policy that installs the app for the organization's users.
- To create the conversation the bot needs `tenantId`, the user's `aadObjectId` or `userId`, and the `serviceUrl`; after creation it posts to the returned `conversationId`. `userId` is unique per bot and user and cannot be reused between bots; `channelId` is global (same page).
- The page says to store the `tenantId` and either the `userId` or `channelId`. The adapter's stored shape is `{ conversationId, serviceUrl, tenantId?, activityId?, replyToId?, teamId?, channelId? }` (`extractTeamsContinuation`). `tenantId`, `activityId` and `replyToId` are optional in that return value.

details.context_before:
### 3.8 Slack: plain links and `block_actions`

- The Slack interaction docs list `block_actions` as the payload for a "Block Kit interactive component", alongside shortcuts, `view_submission` and `view_closed` ([handling user interaction](https://docs.slack.dev/interactivity/handling-user-interaction/)).
details.context_after:
- The Events API `link_shared` event is sent "when a link — matching the registered URL domain your app is setup to track — is posted", not when it is clicked; it also requires a subscription and a registered domain, and apps do not receive it for their own messages ([link_shared](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/link_shared/)). SurveyBeat should register no unfurl domain and subscribe to no `link_shared`.
- **What is not stated.** Slack does not publish a sentence of the form "clicking a plain link sends nothing to the app". The conclusion rests on the payload list above. Unfurling is a separate matter: with `unfurl_links` left on, Slack's servers may fetch the URL (they send no fragment); set `unfurl_links` and `unfurl_media` to false as #295 requires. A live check costs a few minutes: post a message with five plain links to a dev workspace, subscribe the Request URL to a request log, click each, and confirm zero requests.
details.line_prefix: - A button that has a `url` is still an interactive component: "If you're using url, you'll still receive an interaction payload and will need to send an acknowledgement response" ([button element](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/block-elements/button-element/)). **So link buttons do send `block_actions` to our Request URL; plain links do not need to be buttons.** The Chat SDK's `link-button` renders as a `button` with `url` and an `action_id` (`@chat-adapter/slack` `blocks.js`), so it would trigger this; its plain `link` element renders as a `section` with `<url|label>`, which is not an interactive component.

content.text:
Confirmed PR 318 only changes one file.

Planning a waiter script for commit 318. It will wait for commit 317 to finish and for gates and ports to be free before committing and pushing. The script will ignore its own process and check for the 317 script in the process list. If 317 fails permanently, the process disappears and 318 can proceed.

The commit message for PR 318 will be written to /tmp/pr-318-commit.txt. Both scripts will poll every 30 seconds. The busy check already covers vitest and gate.mjs, so 318 will wait while 317 commits. The process check is still needed to prevent both scripts from starting commits simultaneously if they poll at the same instant.

A single sequencer script is cleaner than two separate monitors. It will commit PR 317 first, then PR 318, with retries for port collisions. This eliminates race conditions entirely.

1→#!/usr/bin/env bash
DIR=~/.grok/long-running-background-tasks
LOG=$DIR/commit_317.log
WT=/home/ubuntu/.t3/worktrees/surveybeat-next/t3-c7cc7cf2-3e10cd6c806d0ae2
attempts=0
while :; do
  busy=$(ps -eo cmd | grep -E "scripts/fence/gate.mjs|vitest run --project unit" | grep -v grep | wc -l)
  ports=$(ss -ltn 2>/dev/null | grep -E ':1337|:1338' | wc -l)
  if [ "$busy" -eq 0 ] && [ "$ports" -eq 0 ]; then
10→    attempts=$((attempts + 1))
    (
      set -euo pipefail
      echo "=== attempt $attempts $(date -Is) ==="
      cd "$WT"
      busy2=$(ps -eo cmd | grep -E "scripts/fence/gate.mjs|vitest run --project unit" | grep -v grep | wc -l)
      ports2=$(ss -ltn 2>/dev/null | grep -E ':1337|:1338' | wc -l)
      echo "recheck busy=$busy2 ports=$ports2"
      if [ "$busy2" -ne 0 ] || [ "$ports2" -ne 0 ]; then
        exit 20
20→      fi
      others=$(git status --short | grep -v 'docs/research/r3-mcp-auth.md' || true)
      if [ -n "$others" ]; then
        echo "unexpected files: $others"
        exit 3
      fi
      git add -- docs/research/r3-mcp-auth.md
      git commit -F /tmp/pr-317-commit.txt
      git push -u origin HEAD || git push -v -u origin HEAD
      git rev-parse HEAD
30→      git status --short
      git log -1 --oneline
    ) >> "$LOG" 2>&1
    code=$?
    if [ "$code" -eq 0 ]; then
      sha=$(git -C "$WT" rev-parse --short HEAD)
      echo "ACTION_REQUIRED: COMMIT_OK $sha log=$LOG"
      exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$code" -eq 20 ]; then
40→      printf '%s lost window on attempt %s\n' "$(date -Is)" "$attempts" >> "$LOG"
    elif tail -n 80 "$LOG" | grep -E "already in use|EADDRINUSE|SQLITE_BUSY" >/dev/null; then
      printf '%s port collision on attempt %s (exit %s)\n' "$(date -Is)" "$attempts" "$code" >> "$LOG"
    else
      echo "FAILED: commit exited $code on attempt $attempts, see $LOG"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$attempts" -ge 8 ]; then
      echo "FAILED: gave up after $attempts attempts, see $LOG"
      exit 1
50→    fi
    sleep 20
    continue
  fi
  printf '%s busy=%s port_lines=%s\n' "$(date -Is)" "$busy" "$ports" >> "$LOG"
  sleep 30
done

content.text:
A grep for "busy" would match the script itself if those strings appear in its command line.

The grep won't match the script's own command line. The parent loop is blocked during the git commit subshell. After PR 317 succeeds, PR 318 should be committed immediately to avoid a race window.

The success block will call a new `commit_318` function to start the commit immediately. The busy grep during the pre-check should find nothing. A temporary file will record the commit result.

The parent process will use a `commit_one` helper to run the 318 commit in a subshell with strict error handling. The grep for gate.mjs will not match the script itself because the command line only contains `bash script.sh`.

The `commit_one` helper will verify no other files are modified before staging and committing the target file. It will push the branch and record the commit SHA. The 318 commit will be inlined after the 317 success path rather than extracted into a separate function. If 318 fails on port contention, the script will retry a few times before reporting failure. The 317 commit is already pushed, so the final verdict must still be reported even if 318 fails.

The monitor will receive a single `ACTION_REQUIRED` wake at the end of the script. It will carry both the PR317 SHA and the final PR318 status, either a SHA or `FAIL`. This avoids waking the monitor while PR318 is still running. If PR317 fails, the script exits immediately and never wakes the monitor.

The worktree commit ID differs from the PR head, so the branch may have moved. I will read the footer and test code to decide whether to rename one link or narrow the test query. If the fix is small, I will apply it directly in the 305 worktree and commit.

content.text:
The log ends at the first attempt. The process exited with code 1.

The subshell likely crashed before it could write any further output. The monitor output is needed to confirm the exact failure.

The subshell started successfully because the attempt echo was written. The failure likely occurred during a git command such as status, add, or commit. The script caught the non-zero exit code and printed FAILED to stdout.

The monitor ran for about 9 minutes, so the subshell died immediately after starting. The failure likely stems from `set -euo pipefail` combined with a `ports2=$(ss ... | grep ...)` command that exits when grep finds nothing, causing the assignment to fail and the subshell to exit before it can log the recheck.

The exact failure is now clear. When no gates are running, the `ps` pipeline returns exit code 1 because grep finds nothing. With `pipefail` enabled, that failure aborts the subshell before it can log the recheck.

The outer script catches the non-zero exit code and fails immediately. The outer loop avoids this because it does not use pipefail. The fix is to add `|| true` to the grep commands or disable pipefail for those counts.

The `|| true` fix needs to sit inside the pipeline substitution. Otherwise `pipefail` can short-circuit before `wc` runs, leaving the variable empty.

The `|| true` fix works correctly inside the pipeline substitution. Both scripts will be patched now. The outer loop is unaffected because it does not use pipefail.

The plan is to start the 317 script first, then launch 319 so the holder check succeeds. The 10:21 opus retry will be scheduled next. The 319 script also needs executable permissions.

`wc -l` still runs when `grep` fails in a bash pipeline. The `|| true` makes the assignment succeed and captures the output. The `[ "$ports2" -ne 0 ]` check handles leading spaces in the variable.

The empty output case with `|| true` is safe because `wc -l` prints `0` when `ss` fails. The 317 script's outer loop grep is fine. **Signing in.** `/auth/login` redirects to the app's own form. The form posts the email to `/auth/email-code`, which hands it to Better Auth's verification-code endpoint, and Better Auth mails a six-digit code through the same `EmailSender` the invitations use. `/auth/email-code/verify` exchanges the code for a session: Better Auth writes the `auth_session` row, and its `Set-Cookie` value is put on our response as `__Host-surveybeat-session`. There is no callback route and no state cookie, because nothing redirects off-site, and there is no hosted logout page: sign-out deletes the session row and answers 303 to the app.

Response and answer counts come from Participation records. Answer latency is measured only in tests on a preview stage. Deleting a Person deletes their Participation records, and their anonymous Submissions survive. A member who loses the Edit key cannot change their answers, and that is accepted.

"We do not claim to defend against everything. Database backups are kept for {restoreDays} days so that we can recover from a disaster. Restoring one replays every write, including the one transaction that writes a Participation record and a Submission together. Only named SurveyBeat operators can start a restore, and no Organization admin or Lead can. We also cannot read Cloudflare's own edge logs.",
"traffic is encrypted in transit and storage is encrypted at rest. Only named operators can start a restore, and backups are kept for {restoreDays} days",

- P1 Content gap (B13): the page says nothing about the minimum group size or AI processing. The 30-day backup and "who can trigger a restore" sections are operator detail, ranked above what a member cares about.

In Release 1, a sign-in never creates or joins an Organization on its own. Creating an Organization is self-serve but limited to an operator allowlist, because an open Organization lets anyone have SurveyBeat email arbitrary addresses from our domain, and Cloudflare Email Sending allows transactional mail only. Everyone else joins because a Lead or an Organization admin added them. Adding someone creates a Person (email only) and a Membership, and sends one "you've been added" email of our own. No WorkOS invitation is sent. When that Person first signs in, the Worker links their WorkOS user to the Person by an exact match on a verified email, and only then creates the WorkOS organization membership.

**Threat model.** The Lead, Organization admins, and anyone using the product (UI, API, exports) must never be able to link a member to their Submission, and neither can an operator reading stored data, dumps, or R2 backups. We do **not** claim to defend against an operator who restores the Durable Object to a past moment (point-in-time recovery replays every write, including the one transaction that writes a Participation record and its Submission), reads Cloudflare's internal edge logs, or changes the code to start logging. Against that we use controls instead: only named people can trigger a restore, the privacy page states the 30-day restore window, and code changes on the submission path need review. The answer page's "Your name is never stored with your answers" is true of everything stored.

content.text:
Domain Legal.test.ts should switch to @effect/vitest.

Web legal.test.ts stays on vitest to match the web package. The 24-month retention string remains unchanged. DPA line 107 needs updating to clarify that automatic deletion at the end of the retention period is not yet in place. The Privacy retention cell text is also being reviewed.

The Privacy retention text will state that automatic deletion is not yet in place, so raw data stays with Pulse until then, aggregated results may be kept longer, and backups are retained for restoreDays. The legal entity paragraph will be updated to note that SurveyBeat runs surveybeat.app, the operator's legal name and postal address are not yet published, and GDPR requests should be sent to the email address.

The Terms page will add the operator disclosure to its first paragraph. The DPA introduction will include the same disclosure. The AI paragraph will retain its existing EU and zero-retention details. The Google purpose statement will describe the zero-retention endpoint and specify which data it processes.

AWS AI processing will mirror the Google Cloud endpoint's payload. The Terms AI sentence remains valid once the Privacy Notice is complete. No HTML budget changes are needed for the answer page or emails.

Email snapshots will remain unchanged. The legal.test retention assertion still passes. I will add a test confirming the notice states automatic deletion is not yet in place, and another verifying the AI disclosure mentions scores and Action titles. Existing message keys do not need new entries. The answer page budget test reads rendered HTML and needs no changes. I am ready to commit the 319 worktree.

I will edit the files now. I will commit when ports are free, since pre-commit takes about six minutes. I will reply on GitHub only after the commit is pushed so the comment cites the correct SHA.

I will background the commit so the turn ends immediately. The GitHub replies will be posted after the commit lands. I will not run coderabbit review --agent. The German law sentence stays; owner confirmation is still pending, and I will note that in the user reply.

The glossary test bans "User" and "Survey".

"Question position" is acceptable. "Person" and "Action" are glossary terms. "SurveyBeat" is safe because the regex requires word boundaries. The DPA deletion clause is only checked via placeholder rendering.

A focused test will verify the DPA deletion sentence. The answer page budget is unchanged. The commit message will cover GDPR 305. The privacy notice will drop the automatic deletion promise for raw answers and list the actual AI request fields. The operator's legal name is not in the repo, so the pages will state it is not published yet.

The strings will stay in catalog files. The AWS purpose will be one short sentence. The privacy notice will direct GDPR requests to the email address. The terms and DPA pages will append the same operator disclosure.

The privacy notice will state that raw Answers and comments are retained for {rawMonths} months unless the Organization sets a different period. Automatic deletion is not yet in place. Aggregated Results may be kept longer. Backups are retained for {restoreDays} days.

The DPA will require SurveyBeat to return the Organization's personal data in a machine-readable format upon request when services end. It will delete that data unless the law requires keeping a copy. Backups will overwrite copies as the {restoreDays}-day restore window passes.

Anonymous Submissions are not personal data. They are deleted when the Organization is deleted. AI processing is off by default. When enabled, a request includes Question text, each Question's dimension, score, change, and whether that change is larger than usual, the same figures for each Dimension, redacted comment text tied to a Question position, and the redacted titles of open Actions. It does not include a name, a Person, a Team, a Round, or a time.

The AI service runs in the EU. It keeps no prompts or output. It cannot fall back to another provider. If it is unavailable, the request waits and is retried. The answer page and the Invitation tell members when AI processing is on. The AI service only summarises. Nothing about a Person is decided by it. The Google purpose is a zero-retention endpoint for comment themes and discussion guides.

The AWS purpose will describe a second EU zero-retention endpoint used only when the first cannot serve the request. A domain import fix is also needed. New tests will verify the privacy notice contains the operator disclosure, the automatic deletion disclaimer, and the redacted titles of open Actions. A matching test will be added for the DPA.

The legal-entity name is not in the repo, so I will not invent one. The retention sentence and the AI disclosure do not match the code, and the domain test should use `@effect/vitest`. The web tests already import `vitest`, so that comment does not apply there.

content.text: The commit gate started successfully.

CodeRabbit's four comments are handled. The correction is in the pre-commit gate now and is not merged yet.

- **Legal entity.** No legal name or postal address exists in the repo, so none was invented. The Privacy Notice, Terms, and DPA now say that identity is not published on the page yet, and privacy requests still go to `privacy@surveybeat.app`.
- **Retention.** The notice no longer says raw Answers are deleted after 24 months. It says that period is the policy, automatic deletion is not in place, and the Answers stay with the Pulse until it is. The 30-day backup sentence is unchanged. The DPA says the same about deletion at the end of the retention period.
- **AI disclosure.** A request can include Question text, Question and Dimension scores and changes, whether a change is larger than usual, redacted comment text tied to a Question position, and redacted titles of open Actions. It does not include a name, a Person, a Team, a Round, or a time. The sub-processor rows match that.
- **Test imports.** `packages/domain/src/Legal.test.ts` now uses `@effect/vitest`, like the other domain tests. `apps/web/src/site/legal.test.ts` stays on `vitest`, which is what the other web tests use.

I did not run CodeRabbit's agent command. Opus still reviews this pull request after 10:21 UTC, on the commit that is being pushed now.
